entries.notes: Aalap Davjekar (creative technologist, Goa, India) built bad-ASCII (basci.xyz, May 2026) as a browser-based live visual synthesizer. Key 余项 mechanism: Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion equations seeded by real-time human silhouette edges (via MediaPipe segmentation) — the body outline becomes the mathematical initial condition for biological growth patterns that grow out of the performer and colonize the background. Character systems (ASCII, Chinese glyphs, binary) are used as pure pixel carriers stripped of semantic content — their meaning is chiseled away, leaving shape as remainder. Chinese glyphs alongside ASCII as equivalent visual units is a specific unnamed remainder: neither calligraphy, typography, nor Orientalist symbol use. Self-described as "still a toy" — not gallery-claimed, not in VJ software market, uses ML but entirely distinct from AI-generation discourse. Optical flow orients characters by motion direction; spring/Hooke physics bounces grid on bass hits; simplex noise warp fields; WebSocket multiplayer.

entries.zh_title: Kuro Kasetto：击打与共鸣之间的那个余项
entries.en_title: Kuro Kasetto: The Remainder Between Strike and Resonance
entries.notes: Kuro Kasetto, Mexico (Mexico City). No real name found in public sources — alias only. Instagram @kuro_kasetto, YouTube, Bandcamp kurokasetto.bandcamp.com, Patreon active. Self-description: 'Someone having fun making little sounds.' Setup: (1) Solenoid xylophone: 5 solenoids, Arduino, MIDI from Norns Shield running Bloom script (generative, constantly changing patterns), Chase Bliss MOOD MKII for real-time texture/atmosphere. (2) Generative kalimba setup (similar architecture). (3) Pure Data patches shown alongside xylophone in video. CDM article by Peter Kirn, July 24, 2026 (TODAY — first major English coverage). MATRIXSYNTH post by matrix, April 13, 2026 (robo-xylophone video). Instagram posts 'making the rounds' per Kirn. Performed live at Mexico City's Sinestesia venue (extended set ~July 2025). Music from 2023 (track on Bandcamp) described as 'haunting.' Also works with: Noise+Wingie+SymbioticKit (seen on Instagram), radio frequencies, PlutoSynth. Peter Kirn quotes: 'devices on the very edge of working,' 'more flora than machine,' 'solenoids turned organic,' 'quivers and rustles as if it's more flora than machine.' Bandcamp description: 'Someone having fun making little sounds.' SAE 余项之美 framing: Already-construct 1 = robotic/mechanical percussion tradition (Nancarrow player piano → Pat Metheny Orchestrion → MIDI drum robots); paradigm = machine achieves precision humans cannot; solenoid = precision instrument eliminating human error. Already-construct 2 = ambient music as genre (Eno Music for Airports → 40 years → AI ambient generation 2026 = final brick: text prompt → large model → atmosphere). Both constructs closing from opposite ends. Chisel = remove precision as goal; solenoids 'on the very edge of working'; mechanical unreliability becomes the instrument. Three-layer architecture: Bloom script (digital pattern) → solenoid (mechanical translation) → acoustic body (material response) — none fully controlling the others. Remainder = acoustic-mechanical remainder: spring-return clatter of solenoid mechanism, overtone bloom from too-hard strike, sustain that fades differently each time because the physical world doesn't hold still. Neither sampling (live not recorded) nor synthesis nor drum machine. The specific sound quality at the intersection of electronic timing precision and acoustic material imprecision. Why now: (1) AI ambient generation ('generative ambient = text prompt') closing; once sealed, DIY mechanical generative music practice becomes historical footnote. (2) Robotic music genre consolidating around high-end precision machines, absorbing mechanical from other direction. (3) CDM July 24 2026 = first English naming attempt. Community discovery phase = maximum naming gap. Naming gap: not robotic music (precision required), not ambient (produced/finished), not electroacoustic (academic European tradition), not sound art (gallery-bound), not circuit bending (hardware modification). 'Tiny sounds' = feeling not category. 'More flora than machine' = paradox not category. Category name doesn't exist. Logic still growing: different instruments, evolving apparatus, Patreon active. Zero art-world presence. No image downloaded (proxy blocked). Note: first entry covering solenoid-mechanical-generative-acoustic domain; first entry from Mexico/Latin America; distinct from all prior entries which covered software tools, DSP, hardware synthesis, biological art, scanning cameras, live coding, notation, etc.

entries.zh_title: 谭吉姆：数字音乐从未真正调过的那根弦
entries.en_title: Tānghīm: The String That Digital Music Never Tuned
entries.notes: Khyam Allami (Iraqi-British), Music Intelligence Lab / Center for Advanced Mathematical Sciences, American University of Beirut. Ibrahim El Khansa (co-developer of DiArMaqAr). Presented Beirut July 21, 2026. CDM article Peter Kirn July 22, 2026. Two tools: (1) DiArMaqAr = Digital Arabic Maqām Archive, multilingual (Arabic/English/French) open-source web platform + REST API, GitHub: Music-Intelligence-Lab/DiArMaqAr, URL: diarmaqar.net. Covers tuning systems from al-Kindī (9th century) through 1932 Cairo Congress and 20th-century scholarship. Covers tanāghīm (tuning systems), ajnās (intervals/tetrachords/pentachords), maqāmāt (melodic modes), modulation pathways (intiqalat), all with full bibliographic attribution. (2) Tānghīm = free MIDI plugin, VST3/AU/CLAP macOS/Windows/Linux + Max for Live devices (MPE Receiver + Mono Pitch Bend Receiver for Ableton Live which doesn't support third-party MIDI effects). Version v0.9.0 (pre-1.0). GitHub: Music-Intelligence-Lab/tanghim. Three tuning methods: MTS-ESP (auto-retune compatible synths via shared memory, using ODDSound protocol), MPE (per-note pitch bend polyphonic), Mono PB (single-channel pitch bend, backward-compatible with all MIDI hardware since 1983). Interface: 12 sliders (one per chromatic step, with snap markers and cents readouts, IPN labels, solfège, PAO names), expandable to full width for two-dīwān view, 8 preset slots (MIDI-mappable, Program-Change-automatable), built-in triangle oscillator for audition, Heptatonic mode (remaps white keys to maqām degrees for easy play), reference pitch control (Hz/cents), MIDI drag-export of current maqām notes. Etymology: tānghīm = Arabic maṣdar (verbal noun) for the act of intoning or setting pitch (the active process); distinct from dūzān = mechanical string tuning before performance (from Ottoman Turkish düzen). DiArMaqAr API: Tānghīm queries it live, caches locally, update button shows when archive has changed. SAE 余项之美 framing: Already-construct 1 = MIDI 12-TET (1983 spec: pitch = integer 0-127, 100 cents/semitone; hardened through all DAW/synth/controller hardware for 40 years; the invisible substrate of all digital music production). Already-construct 2 = tasyīk/tashrīq: since 1980s digital Arabic keyboards, the standard digital workaround for maqām was lowering one note by 50 cents (approximating a 'quarter tone sīkāh'); this became the default form of 'digital Arabic music' — itself a construct, replacing full intonational practice with a single fixed deviation. Chisel 1 = DiArMaqAr API: formally encodes 1000+ years of tuning theory as machine-readable data. Chisel 2 = Tānghīm: three methods to bypass 12-TET floor without requiring host DAW changes; inserts maqām data into any production workflow. Remainder 1 = full intonational body of Arabic maqām: al-Kindī through Cairo Congress interval structures, always in practice, never in digital infrastructure. Remainder 2 = live intonation (tānghīm vs dūzān): maqām is not a fixed pitch set but a living practice of continuous adjustment; all prior tuning tools only did dūzān (set and lock); Tānghīm's draggable sliders point toward tānghīm (the active intonation); this remainder is not yet fully captured even by Tānghīm (slider interface is a gesture, not the act itself). Naming gap: not 'microtonal' (Western-centric, 12-TET as baseline); not 'world music plugin' (colonialist frame); not 'tuning software' (misses liveness); not 'maqam plugin' (tasyīk approximation = existing digital maqam practice, which this explicitly replaces). Peter Kirn: 'The computer can do better; we can do better.' = acknowledgment of remainder, not category name. Kirn also: 'I haven't gotten to talk to Khyam yet' (July 22 article) — naming conversation just beginning. Sami Shumays (Palestinian-American scholar/musician) raised same tuning-system accessibility critique years prior (CDM: 'Pitch is Political'). Why now: AI music generation (Suno/Udio) nearly entirely 12-TET corpora; 'AI music = 12-TET music' equation closing; Arabic maqām becoming labeled exception rather than active remainder. v0.9.0 = pre-1.0, actively growing. DiArMaqAr API = live, other tools can build on it. No image downloaded (proxy blocked). Zero art-world presence (academic music research). Do not repeat: first entry covering Arabic/Middle Eastern tuning theory as digital remainder / 12-TET MIDI construct / live intonation vs static tuning / tasyīk construct; distinct from all prior entries which covered DAW tools, hardware synthesis, visual performance, notation, generative art, etc.

entries.zh_title: 扫描仪始终是台相机
entries.en_title: Project Gigapixel: The Scanner Was Always a Camera
entries.notes: Yannick Richter (GitHub/Hackaday.io handle: Gigawipf). Project Gigapixel: DIY linear scanning camera built from an Epson V370 flatbed scanner's CCD array, presented at Hackaday Europe 2026 (July 2026). Hackaday.io project started August 2025. Hackaday article by Zoe Skyforest, July 20, 2026. Sensor: Sony ILX561K linear CCD, 12 lines (RGB x2x2 Main+Sub), 122,400 total pixels, driven by S7R77S14F00A100 ADC+clock gen chip. Resolution: 80,000 x 40,160 pixels (~3.2 gigapixels, 16-bit true color) with medium-format 6x7 lens. Also tested at 15360 x 40160 (600MP) as documented image. Mounted on 100mm linear drive; controlled via Raspberry Pi 5 + RP2350. Pentax medium-format lens. Preview camera: standard RPi camera for live view (linear sensor cannot provide live preview). Hardware: entire original scanner circuit replaced, not 'scanner in a box' approach. Key feature: can read 0603 SMD resistor values in final crops. Flickr album of sample images available. SAE 余项之美 framing: Already-construct = flatbed scanner as document reproduction apparatus (35+ years, Epson/Canon/HP, entire product definition is 'faithfully copy flat objects to pixels'; all specs/software/calibration serve this definition). Chisel = reverse-engineering sensor protocol, removing from document-reproduction context, mounting behind photographic lens. Remainder #1 = imaging capability of linear CCD (always present, suppressed by 'document scanner' product definition). Remainder #2 = scanning temporality as photographic proposition: linear sensor must traverse focal plane over seconds-to-minutes; only what holds still can be photographed; this creates a specific photographic stance: 'the camera photographs what the world is patient enough to offer.' Why now: AI image synthesis in 2026 can generate 'a high-resolution photograph of anything' — but scanner camera only captures what actually exists and actually holds still; this temporal commitment is the remainder AI cannot fake. Naming gap: not scanography (no glass/no lens — completely different practice where objects placed directly on flatbed); not gigapixel stitching (not multiple shots merged); not DIY camera (label hides the structural proposition); not document scanner (former identity). Hackaday Europe conference was in Germany, July 2026. Hackaday commenter 'Dude' misidentified project as 'gigapixel stitching was all the rage 20 years ago' — demonstrating the naming gap is wide open. Zero art-world presence (hardware hacking community). Logic still growing: project was started August 2025, actively developed, presented publicly July 2026. Note: first entry in series covering scanner/camera/photography hardware domain; distinct from all prior entries which covered audio tools, creative coding, bio-art, demoscene, net art, typography.

entries.zh_title: Schwung：产品边界之下，Linux 一直在等
entries.en_title: Schwung: Below the Product Boundary, the Linux Was Always There
entries.notes: Charles Vestal (charlesvestal on GitHub), not a self-described developer — uses AI tools (Claude, Codex) for implementation under human supervision. Project origin: 'extending-move' (May 2025, CDM article by Peter Kirn), then 'Move Everything' (February 2026 launch per Synthanatomy), then renamed 'Schwung' (German: momentum/swing). Website: schwung.dev. GitHub: charlesvestal/schwung. 397 stars, 54 forks, 2187 commits, 86 releases as of Jun 25 2026 (v0.11.4). Discord: discord.gg/GHWaZCC9bQ. Built on top of Move Anything project (bobbydigitales) which originally reverse-engineered SSH access. Technical: Ableton Move runs on Raspberry Pi CM4, Linux OS, SSH accessible over WiFi. Schwung installs via single curl command over SSH. Shadow UI runs alongside stock Move's native system, sharing same hardware (display, pads, knobs, buttons) via unclaimed button combinations. Module catalog (schwung.dev/catalog.html) installable via Schwung Manager (http://move.local:7700) or desktop installer. Module categories: (1) Sound generators: Dexed (DX7 FM), Surge XT hybrid, OB-Xd (Oberheim OB-X), Hera (Juno-60+chorus), Braids/Plaits (Mutable Instruments), Osirus (Access Virus), RaffoSynth (Moog Ladder), SF2 SoundFont, Famicom/Game Boy sound sources, CLAP plugin host for Linux CLAP plugins. (2) Effects: CloudSeed algorithmic reverb, NAM neural amp modeler, PSX Verb (PS1-style), Verglas (Clouds granular), Tapescam (tape saturation), Junologue Chorus, Space Delay (RE-201). (3) Overtake modules/tools: DJ Deck (CDJ-style), Eucalypso (Euclidean sequencer), Stems (on-device stem separation), AutoSample (multisampling external MIDI gear via FFT spectral loop detection), Radio Garden (global radio stations real-time sampling), YouTube audio sampling, AirPlay input, on-device audio editor (trim/slice), time-stretching with pitch shift, skip-back recorder (last 30 seconds), screen reader with TTS. (4) Accessibility: screen reader makes Move first standalone groovebox with blind/visually impaired support — text-to-speech, adjustable speed/pitch/volume, runs on device without extra tools. Schwung v0.8.4 (March 2026) = Auto Sampler + LFOs + song mode. v0.11.4 (Jun 25, 2026) = latest. Synthanatomy article March 16, 2026. nedavine note.com article April 24, 2026 (English translation). CDM extending-move article May 30, 2025. Charles Vestal quote: 'This is a hack in the true sense of the word. It is not stable, or generally usable as a daily driver, but it is interesting, and super fun.' Synth Anatomy commenter: 'Ableton needs to hire this guy.' Vestal reply: 'I try to be very up front about all of that! This is a bunch of experiments and I'm learning a lot, but this is both based on the techniques in the Move Anything project that opened up the device using real human code, and a lot of AI-coded extensions.' SAE 余项之美 framing: Already-construct = 'consumer music hardware as closed system' (30 years: manufacturer defines features = hardware potential; Move's product positioning as 'sketchbook' is the latest instantiation, not technical limitation). Second already-construct = 'Linux substrate as infrastructure' (the floor Ableton software runs on, not territory). Chisel #1 = SSH access (Move's Linux OS was always accessible, never locked). Chisel #2 = Shadow UI concept: don't replace the construct, run alongside it — parallel layer sharing same hardware via unclaimed button combinations. Remainder #1 = compute substrate: CM4's ability to run Surge XT/Dexed/CloudSeed etc. was always present, declared nonexistent by product boundary. Remainder #2 = accessibility territory: screen reader, TTS, blind musician support — never hardware-blocked, never entered product definition. Remainder #3 = radio/streaming tools: Radio Garden, YouTube sampling, AirPlay — all via built-in WiFi, always possible. 'Structurally second-order remainder': Move's WiFi (designed for Ableton cloud sync and MIDI) generates a remainder (arbitrary internet audio access) that itself was never acknowledged. Why now: Official absorption ongoing — Move 1.5 added slicing (Schwung first), Move 2.0 added audio tracks, Ableton Extensions API in Live 12.4.5, RNBO Move Takeover (Cycling '74, March 2026) is official answer to 'run custom synths on Move.' Each update narrows the gap. Naming gap maximum right now: not custom firmware / not jailbreak / not plugin / not DIY audio / not open-source hardware. 'Unofficial framework for running custom instruments, effects, and controllers on Ableton Move' = outline drawn via negations because affirmative category doesn't exist. 'Schwung' = metaphor (momentum/swing), not category. No art-world presence. Logic actively growing: 86 releases, Discord active, CLAP plugin host expanding. AI-assisted development disclosed explicitly in repo and by Vestal in interviews. Do not repeat: first entry covering 'product definition as construct / hardware substrate as remainder / Shadow UI concept / consumer groovebox Linux ecosystem' territory; distinct from all prior entries which covered synthesis tools, performance software, audio routing, physical instruments, screensavers, live coding, bio-art, DAW plugins.

entries.zh_title: Void LinkAudio：去掉中心之后，剩下来的是什么
entries.en_title: Void LinkAudio: What Remains When the Hub Is Gone
entries.notes: Julien Bayle (gluon on GitHub), Structure Void, Ableton Certified Trainer and Max Certified Trainer. VOID LinkAudio: open-source multi-host integration of Ableton Link Audio protocol. Released v0.2.0 May 3 2026 (CDM article by Peter Kirn May 3 2026), two days before Ableton Live 12.4 official release (May 5 2026). Hosts supported: Max/MSP externals (void.linkaudio.send~ and void.linkaudio.receive~, full Max package with help patchers and refpages), Pure Data vanilla 0.56-2+, TouchDesigner, VCV Rack, openFrameworks (separate repo: gluon/ofxAbletonLinkAudio), VST/AU/CLAP plugins. v0.3.0: added Linux support for VCV Rack 2 and Pure Data (x86_64 and ARM64). Pre-built binaries for macOS Universal and Windows x64; notarized for macOS. MIT-licensed open source; Gumroad bundle pay-what-you-want. GitHub: gluon/Void-LinkAudio. Ableton Link Audio protocol: extension to Ableton Link (P2P tempo/beat/phase sync, embedded in hundreds of apps and hardware), adds sample-accurate audio buffer transmission between Link peers over local network. Live 12.4 shipped May 5 2026 with official Link Audio support. Julien Bayle disclosure on LLM use: 'The architecture, audio path, threading model, and DSP decisions are mine. On the security side: code is fully open source under GPL-2.0; Mac binaries notarized; networking layer is Ableton's own Link Audio reference implementation.' Community discussion: Cycling '74 forum (VoidLinkAudio thread), Pure Data forum (pdpatchrepo), KVR Audio forum thread. SAE 余项之美 framing: Already-construct #1 = DAW as audio hub (30 years: all audio through central DAW, instruments/effects as nodes, star topology — Pro Tools 1991 to Ableton Live 2026). Already-construct #2 = OS virtual audio driver as inter-app proxy (BlackHole/Loopback/Soundflower): artists running multiple tools simultaneously route audio through OS-level virtual device — structurally identical to DAW hub, just at OS level. Already-construct #3 = professional network audio (Dante, AVB, NetJack): complex, driver-dependent, broadcast-oriented. All three hardened by 2026. Chisel = Link Audio protocol at creative tool level: P2P audio over LAN, no drivers, no complex config, just 'tools in the same room'. Bayle implements it across 6+ hosts simultaneously. Remainder #1 = the tool boundary itself: the zone where VCV Rack's modular signal crosses into TouchDesigner's visual environment crosses into Max's algorithmic space — each crossing is a compositional event. This 'between-tools territory' always existed (artists always ran multiple tools) but was always infrastructure friction, never material, because hub mediated everything. Remainder #2 = routing topology as compositional parameter: without any gravitational center, the graph of which tool sends to which becomes a creative decision, like patch cables in modular synthesis. Why now: Live 12.4 official release (May 5) installs Live as natural gravitational center of any Link Audio network — most users will configure all tools sending to/from Live, recapturing hub structure in new form. Window of visible peer topology was exactly the two-day gap before Live 12.4 launch, plus the period before ecosystem settles. Naming gap: Kirn says 'fits some territory in between JACK and Dante' — the gap between two negations is exactly the unnamed remainder. Not 'routing' (implies single host), not 'network audio' (professional connotation), not 'multi-app workflow' (sequential not simultaneous), not 'sync' (Link tempo sync is already named). 'Creative peer network' and 'tool boundary zone' are invented descriptors, not received categories. Logic actively growing: v0.3.0 Linux, active forum discussion, more hosts possible. No image downloaded (proxy blocked). Zero art-world presence. Domain: first entry covering cross-tool audio networking as creative medium / routing topology as instrument; distinct from all prior entries. Do not repeat: focus was the DAW-as-hub construct / OS-driver-as-proxy construct / Link Audio as peer dissolving both / tool boundary zone as remainder / routing graph as compositional material.

entries.project_name: Evan Montpellier / Nicolas Bernier / Laboratoire formes • ondes / SIGN/e
entries.zh_title: SIGN/e：DAW 时间轴第一次向外说话
entries.en_title: SIGN/e: The First Time the DAW Timeline Spoke Outward
entries.notes: Evan Montpellier (programmer), Nicolas Bernier (professor, LFO-lab director), Laboratoire formes • ondes, Département de musique numérique, Université de Montréal. Co-directors also: Myriam Boucher, Dominic Thibault, Pierre Michaud. SIGN/e = Symbol-based Interface for Graphic Notation/Edition. Free Max for Live plugin suite. v1.0.0 released May 12, 2026 on GitHub (LFO-lab/SIGNe). CDM article by Peter Kirn May 15, 2026. UdeM institutional press release May 21, 2026. Paper: 'Contemporary notation framework: approaches, encoding and medium' by Pierre-Luc Lecours and Nicolas Bernier, Organised Sound (Cambridge), Feb 24, 2026. TENOR international debut Vienna May 2026. Download URL: https://lfo-lab.ca/notation-performative-en. Student composition: Alexandre Sasset-Blouin (master's student, UdeM Faculty of Music), harp piece with animated score — split-screen video shows composer and harpist synchronized with dynamic graphic score. Summer 2026 collaboration: Nicolas Bernier + guitarist Simon Trottier, piece for folk guitar sampled in real-time with SIGN/e score. Technical: places PNG images on Ableton Live timeline, animates them (rotation, translation, etc.); symbols represent performative gestures not sound events — color identifies which parameter to manipulate, shape specifies action (line=continuous movement, circle=brief action). Previously, graphic score workflow: draw in Illustrator, export, manually align against DAW — 'if a symbol needs to be shifted even just one pixel to the left, they have to re-export the whole thing' (Bernier). Bernier's core insight: electronic music notation must shift focus from sound to performer movement/gesture — 'controlled accidents' (sonic surprises from complex processing chains) cannot be notated in CWN. SAE 余项之美 framing: Already-construct 1 = CWN as universal score document separate from performance software (500 years, Sibelius/Finale/Dorico extensions). Already-construct 2 = DAW session as closed inward-pointing electronic performance (Ableton Live session plays through speakers; no live performers; DAW=work not score). Already-construct 3 = avant-garde graphic notation tradition (Cage, Feldman, Cardew 1950s-70s) = art-world-named historical artifacts, museumified, canonized. Chisel = SIGN/e embeds animated notation inside Ableton Live session: score is inside the DAW, not a separate document; score is animated not static; DAW timeline now points outward toward live performers. Remainder #1 = animated graphic notational primitives (rotating circle, scrolling line) — new formal elements suited to 'controlled accidents' that CWN constitutionally cannot capture. Remainder #2 = DAW timeline as shared temporal medium between electronics and live performers — conductor/score/performance machine sharing one timeline; latent in every DAW since 1990s, never actualized. Why now: AI music generation closing 'electronic music = closed product = no live performers' equation; TENOR 2026 and Organised Sound paper beginning naming but not complete; summer 2026 collaboration ongoing; logic still growing. Naming gap: not VJ tool (score for performers not audience visualization), not notation software (no CWN, animated, embedded in performance), not graphic score software (Illustrator export workflow is graphic score software, SIGN/e is different), not Max for Live visual device (has compositional and performative grammar). CDM: 'a bit like you're playing in an enchanted music academy haunted by the ghost of Oskar Fischinger' — invented metaphor because no name exists. No image downloaded (proxy blocked). Zero art-world presence (music research/academic world, not contemporary art market). Note: distinct from all prior entries which covered audio synthesis tools, DAW plugins, instrument hardware, screensavers, biological art, demoscene. First entry covering the electronic-music-notation / score-embedded-in-DAW / performer-facing DAW domain.

entries.project_name: Sinevibes / Artemiy Pavlov / Quarta for Korg NTS-3
entries.zh_title: Sinevibes Quarta：四象限里凿去制造商的那份领地
entries.en_title: Sinevibes Quarta: The Territory in the Four-Zone Pad
entries.notes: Artemiy Pavlov, raised in Kharkiv, runs Sinevibes solo from Kyiv. Sinevibes builds DSP effects for KORG's logue platform (NTS-1, NTS-1 mkII, NTS-3, Minilogue XD, etc.). KORG logue SDK: open C SDK allowing third-party developers to write and load custom oscillators and effects onto KORG hardware via USB. NTS-3: Nu:Tekt DIY solder kit (~$100), X/Y touchpad form factor (kaoss pad), pocket-sized, runs logue SDK custom effects. Quarta released July 2026 ($29; bundle with Cache $49). Divides X/Y pad into 4 zones (2×2 grid). Each zone can be configured with one of 10 DSP algorithms: SVF low-pass/high-pass/band-pass/notch/peaking, phaser (8-stage all-pass), comb positive/negative feedback, Bode frequency shifter, sample rate converter/resampler. Also: random algorithm mode (dice on touch), gesture modes (fixed value/random/directional L-R or T-B/bar animations over 1-2 bars), all configurable on-device. CDM review by Peter Kirn July 2, 2026; Synth Anatomy, Matrixsynth, Sonicstate also covered. Peter Kirn note: 'it's funny how little Korg talks about the NTS-3 or its expandable effects.' Artemiy showed at Superbooth 2026 at both KORG (Z440) and Dreadbox (W425) booths. SAE 余项之美 framing: Already-construct = hardware effects device as closed algorithm container (KP1 1999 → KP3 → KP-Quartz; all hardware pedals/processors; manufacturer defines sound ceiling). X/Y pad form always technically capable of mapping categories not just parameters — but closed algorithm layer prevented it. Chisel = logue SDK opens algorithm layer; any C developer can define what the hardware does; NTS-3 sound identity no longer set by Korg. Remainder #1 = X/Y touchpad as algorithm navigation space: Quarta's 4-zone grid deploys the coordinate space to navigate between DSP categories (not just parameters within one DSP). Cross boundary = switch sound logic. Move within zone = modulate parameters. This was latent in the form since 1999. Remainder #2 = 'community-defined hardware sound identity' as entire unnamed territory: commercial hardware (KORG product) + open algorithm layer = ecosystem where manufacturer made hardware but community defines what it sounds like. Korg doesn't acknowledge or market this. Sinevibes is the most prolific developer. No institutional support. No category name. Naming gap: not KAOSS Pad (sounds third-party defined), not plugin (physical hardware), not DIY audio (you soldered it, but DSP is specialist work), not open-source hardware (KORG corporate, only SDK open), not modular (no voltage/cables). CDM's description: 'pocket live/DJ effect' = performance description not structural. Why now: logue SDK maintained but invisible in marketing; Artemiy operating from Kyiv without institutional support; AI effect generation tools consolidating 'what an effect sounds like' space; window before community-DSP-for-hardware-becomes-historical-footnote. No images downloaded (proxy blocked). Zero art-world presence. Logic actively growing: Artemiy adding algorithms, platform expanding.

entries.notes: shibco (Cade), Berlin. GitHub: shibco/ableton-linux. Published July 15 2026. CDM article by Peter Kirn July 15, 2026. Wine patches enabling Ableton Live 12 Suite + Beta, Max for Live, Push 1+2 on Linux. Feature list: WineASIO→JACK/PipeWire at 256 frames low-latency, HiDPI auto-detect, VST3/JUCE/OpenGL window rendering, device recovery (audio and MIDI survive disconnect/reconnect), dark/light theme follows system, native file dialogs via XDG portal, system font rendering, Ableton Extensions SDK support, VST-specific fixes (Autuira/Pianoteq/SWAM/KORG), reproducible builds. AI disclosure in repo: local models (Qwen 3.6) and Claude Opus used for QA testing, documentation, build pipeline setup. Also separately: BEEFY-JOE/AbletonLiveOnLinux (different repo, community documentation resource for running Ableton on Linux). SAE 余项之美 framing: Already-construct = commercial music production platform triangle (macOS/Windows/iOS, 25 years of sedimentation; every major DAW, plugin, hardware manufacturer targets this triangle; 'music production platform' = commercial OS with vendor relationship). Chisel = Wine compatibility layer: not emulation but re-implementation of Windows API surface; shibco's patches complete Wine's infrastructure for Live's specific requirements. Remainder #1 = the territory of music production after platform-as-vendor-product assumption is removed: OS belongs to no corporation, audio routing via community infrastructure (JACK/PipeWire), commercial + open-source tools coexist without hierarchy — unnamed category. Remainder #2 (second-order) = the accumulation logic: 25 years of Linux audio development (kernel improvements, ALSA, JACK, PipeWire, Wine evolution) built for no goal related to Ableton Live, arriving as infrastructure remainder that suddenly enables it. Why now: RAMageddon hardware crisis (2026), Apple/Microsoft AI integration via proprietary OS-locked APIs, platform dependency risk acute, Kirn explicitly notes institutional uncertainty. Naming gap: not 'emulation' (wrong technical term), not 'Linux DAW' (not built for Linux), not 'Wine gaming' (different requirements/culture), not 'Ableton for Linux' (no such product). No art-world presence. Logic actively growing: Push 3 not yet supported, feature list expanding, institutional pressure building toward official support. No image downloaded (proxy blocked). entries.zh_title: Isadora：让肉身驾驭声音的那片领地
entries.en_title: Isadora: The Territory Where Body Conducts Sound
entries.notes: Mark Coniglio (b. 1961, Omaha, NE), music composition degree CalArts 1989 (with Morton Subotnick). Created MidiDancer 1989: wireless angular-change body joint sensor → MIDI real-time. Co-developed Interactor with Subotnick (graphic programming for real-time MIDI/media manipulation). Co-founder Troika Ranch (with choreographer Dawn Stoppiello, NYC-based dance/theater group integrating music/dance/theater/interactive digital media). TroikaTronix: Neue Schönhauser Straße 12, 10178 Berlin, Germany. Isadora: named after Isadora Duncan. 100+ universities use Isadora in curriculum. Users include Laurie Anderson, Judith Jamison. IzzyCast: companion tool for remote performance via Isadora. Isadora 4.5 released July 14, 2026. Key 4.5 additions: multichannel audio I/O, VST3 plugin support with interactive control (including real-time parameter control from Actors), extensive audio playback (real-time waveforms, loop controls, volume, panning), advanced interactive mixing, MIDI generator plugins with tempo/time signature, Actors for audio level watching, frequency watching, audio-to-text transcription, programmatic control of routing/mixing settings, beautiful audio routing matrix. Also: Wave GPU actor (rippled textures). CDM article by Peter Kirn, July 14, 2026. Quote: 'It's the opposite of the current world of AI, because it says the open-ended generative powers of the computer are something you can use live — to play.' Peter Kirn personally used Interactor in high school at Oberlin (dragged a Mac tower onstage with a Disklavier). SAE 余项之美 framing: Already-construct 1 = DAW timeline paradigm (horizontal ruler, events placed, rendered — even Ableton Live is a timeline host). Already-construct 2 = audio-visual split in interactive performance (Max/Pd or DAW handles audio; TouchDesigner/vvvv/Resolume handles visuals; they communicate via OSC/MIDI but are separate). Already-construct 3 = AI creative tools as 'describe → generate content' formula (hardening in 2026). Chisel = Isadora's entire architecture: scene-based, condition-based, Actors respond to performance triggers (body sensors, MIDI, camera tracking, OSC); organizes media by dramaturgy not timeline; now extended to audio with 4.5 so DAW intermediary is removed. Remainder = the territory where dance and sound are genuinely one thing — same interactive logic, same conditions, same body-driven grammar governing image and sound simultaneously. This territory has existed since MidiDancer 1989 but has never been formally named. Dance/theater world uses Isadora but is invisible to music tech press (CDM rarely covers Isadora). Why now: (1) 4.5 just released July 14 2026, removing the DAW-as-intermediary; (2) AI 'generate from prompt' construct sealing creative imagination space in 2026; (3) TouchDesigner (VC-backed, Nvidia AI integration) absorbing interactive visual performance space — Isadora is last major tool maintaining independence and dramaturgy philosophy; (4) naming gap at maximum width: 'interactive nonlinear host that responds to performance' (Kirn's invented phrase). Naming gap: not DAW (no timeline), not VJ tool (not visuals-first), not Max/Pd (not instrument-building — Isadora is condition-programming for performance), not TouchDesigner (dramaturgy/theater vs data/installation), not media server (interactive not playback), not AI tool (the opposite). Name itself is a remainder: a dancer's name, not an algorithm name. No image downloaded (proxy blocked). Zero art-world presence (theater/dance world, not contemporary art market). Structural aliveness: 4.5 just released, active development, community growing, add-on ecosystem (Werkstatt). Do not repeat: first entry covering interactive media performance / dance-technology / body-as-conductor territory; distinct from all prior entries which covered audio synthesis, VCV Rack, browser art, programming languages, etc.

entries.zh_title: SocaLabs Identity：当波形变成公式，剩下来的是什么
entries.en_title: SocaLabs Identity: What Remains When the Waveform Becomes a Formula
entries.notes: SocaLabs Identity by FigBug (Victoria BC; KVR member since 2005; also runs refx.com and rabiensoftware.com). Released July 7, 2026 for KVR Developer Challenge 2026 — his first entry. Developer's own account: 'I started working on it 6 years ago, and it mostly sat in a dusty corner until I finally got the motivation to finish it. I have no idea if this is musically useful or just a nerdy experiment I wanted to try.' Core feature: two formula oscillators — instead of waveform dropdown, user types mathematical expression (sine(x), saw(x), triangle(x), square(x), pulse(x, pwm), and arbitrary combinations/products/nestings). Anti-aliasing applied internally. Sub-oscillator and noise generators support formula oscillators. Additional: asymmetric shaping, wave-folding, phase manipulation, two multimode filters (LP/HP/BP/Notch, 12/24dB), four MSEG LFOs, three ADSR envelopes, modulation matrix with drag-and-drop, 11 reorderable effects (gate/chorus/distortion/delay/reverb/EQ/filter/etc.), arpeggiator, four macro knobs, per-voice vibrato, MPE support, analog drift. Free, VST3/AU/LV2/CLAP on macOS/Windows/Linux. Lime green GUI (developer's own design, not AI-generated). Reviewed by Synth Anatomy July 8, 2026. SAE 余项之美 framing: Already-construct = the standard waveform palette (sine/saw/triangle/square/pulse) naturalized over 60 years of synthesis into categorical given — waveform as acoustic fact not mathematical choice. Chisel = replacing dropdown with text field, making visible that saw(x) and saw(x/2)*sine(x*3) are the same class of object. Dissolves waveform-as-type frame by making formula the interface. Remainder = (1) gap between typed formula and heard sound — formula is score, signal chain rewrites it through folding/asymmetry/filters/drift; (2) creator's own uncertainty — six-year dusty corner, 'nerdy experiment,' cannot name its category. Why now: AI-assisted synthesis absorbing formula-sound relationship into black box (window closing). Naming gap: 'formula oscillator synthesizer' has no prior genre; press settles for functional descriptors; creator self-describes as experiment. KVR forum 7 posts. Zero art-world presence. Distinct from prior entries: first entry covering synthesis waveform-formula category; distinct from Thorn Audio Splines (spline-as-voltage / curve-as-sound domain).

entries.zh_title: Splines：凿去中介之后，曲线剩了下来
entries.en_title: Thorn Audio Splines: When the Curve No Longer Serves
entries.notes: Thorn Audio Splines by Hallvard Kristiansen (Norwegian engineer, repair technician at Schneidersladen Berlin, prior module: VCLFO). Released May 2026. 10HP Eurorack module. Core: Kochanek-Bartels cubic Hermite spline generator (same spline family used in 3D Studio Max, Newtek Lightwave, Pixar animation). 16 user-configurable nodes. Three primary parameters: tension (severity of curve between nodes), continuity (sharpness of angle at node), bias (asymmetric tension distribution). Additional: wavefolding, clipping (hard/soft/fold/rectify/comparator/bitcrush), zoom/scroll, quantizer with Scala file support. Frequency range: very slow LFO to 20kHz audio. 6 CV inputs (for all parameters), 3 CV outputs. Built-in oscilloscope for all 6 CV inputs. Hardware: ESP32 S3, 1.8" color LCD display, Kailh Choc v2 key switches, USB-C. UI design: Joni Caparas. Price: 359€/$413. CDM review by Peter Kirn May 26, 2026. Synth Anatomy review June 5, 2026. SAE 余项之美 framing: Already-construct = spline as DAW automation infrastructure (30 years: every DAW automation lane, Illustrator Pen tool Bézier splines, game engine Catmull-Rom easing, motion graphics). Spline always serves something else — it is transparent to itself. Chisel = remove the intermediary parameter layer: in DAW performer→automation curve→parameter→sound; in Splines performer→spline curve→voltage→sound. Curve and sound are directly identical. Remainder = the aesthetic texture of mathematical interpolation itself — Kochanek-Bartels tension (brittle precision of high tension vs liquid low), continuity (smooth vs sharp tangent), bias asymmetry, wavefolded polynomial textures — always present in every DAW automation lane but never heard as sound because never the sound. Why now: AI automation curve generation becoming standard DAW feature (window closing); Freya Holmér spline math YouTube spreading (naming approaching). Naming gap: not function generator (generates pre-defined not user-defined curves), not MSEG (always in service of parameter), not oscillator (more than waveform), not LFO (more than modulation). Peter Kirn literally invents a 5-item function list because category doesn't exist. No art world presence. Logic still growing: Scala tuning ongoing, CDM promises more coverage. Do not repeat: first entry covering mathematical interpolation / spline-as-aesthetic-object domain; distinct from all prior entries which covered signal processing, bio-art, voice synthesis, programming languages, canvases, screensavers, etc.

entries.zh_title: NMS：制作与演奏之间那个从未分离过的地带
entries.en_title: New Modular System: The Territory Where Making and Playing Were Never Separate
entries.notes: Tim Exile (born Ben Thomson), UK-based musician and instrument builder. Philosophy degree Durham University (dissertation: difference between music and noise). Prior work: Flesh (Native Instruments, 2015), Scapeshift and Finalist (Reaktor-based tools). New Modular System (NMS): Reaktor 6 (full license required, not Player) patchable environment for building playable instruments. Announced April 14 2026 (Sonic State teaser), CDM article by Peter Kirn April 28 2026, Synthtopia May 1 2026, Gearnews headline 'The First Of Its Kind?' Current status: working prototype, £49 early access (full version free at launch, £69). Prototype contains: 5 ready-to-play patches, 9 instrument modules (Chowning FM synth, Sawbird subtractive, Aaron snare, Duffy kick, Handmaid clap, Hattersly hi-hat, Skin percussion, Schaefer experimental sampler [named after Pierre Schaeffer], Didimidi MIDI generator), 4 FX modules (Baikal reverb, Pyongyang dub delay, Roisin triggered resonator, Sinkhole filter glitch), 11 controller modules (Loop Pack, Macros, Mixer, Transport & Scale, Wander [generative, plays itself forever], Patterns, Builder Macros, Builder Tools, Chaos, Launch Control XL, Patterns/Collections/Sets). Launch video title: 'Music production feels pointless now. So I built THIS instead.' NMS website has whitepaper PDF (part 1 of 2) explaining the philosophy and roadmap. Key phrase: 'Build it. Play it. Stay in flow.' Roadmap: SDK, full UI redesign, complete pitch/scale engine, Scapeshift/Finalist mixing/mastering engine, send/return channels, full per-module bypass/solo/lock. SAE 余项之美 framing: Already-construct = DAW production paradigm (compose→arrange→mix→master→release, hardened since late 1990s), now accelerated by AI to complete colonization (prompt→track). Internal assumption of DAW paradigm: building instrument and playing instrument are SEQUENTIAL phases (build first, map second, play third). Chisel = Controller Module concept: drop one in, instrument is immediately playable; you never exit 'build mode' to enter 'play mode' because these modes were always fictitious. Remainder = the mode of music-making where building and playing were never distinct — what Pierre Schaeffer did with tape (Schaefer module named after him), what live electronic performers do when configuring systems on stage, what modular synthesis was before production culture absorbed it — specifically: 'the dialogue with the patch — hearing what it wants, responding, shaping it back' (Tim's own words). Naming gap: not DAW (no timeline), not VST (not in a track), not Eurorack (no physical rack/cables), not sequencer (controllers generate playing not sequences), not production tool (no production pipeline). 'New Modular System' = adjective + generic noun, names nothing. Gearnews: 'The First Of Its Kind?' No existing category. Whitepaper required to explain it. Structural aliveness: prototype/pre-launch, SDK not yet released, UI not finalized, pitch/scale engine in development, community module building not yet possible. Zero art-world presence. Why now: AI music production has sealed the DAW production paradigm so completely that the remainder is at maximum visibility; the 'music production feels pointless now' crisis is acute in 2026; once NMS is named/absorbed into 'post-AI human musicianship' discourse it becomes construct. No image downloaded (proxy blocked). Note: this entry is the first covering the 'build/play unification' territory; distinct from all prior entries which covered specific instrument design or tool paradigms. Do not repeat: focus was the build/play distinction as the hidden assumption of DAW paradigm, chiseled by Controller Module concept, remainder = the dialogue-with-patch mode of music-making that predates and exceeds the production pipeline.

entries.zh_title: ShinRonin：被允许出轨的那个路由矩阵
entries.en_title: ShinRonin: The Routing Matrix That's Allowed to Misbehave
entries.notes: Audio Damage (founded 2002 by Chris Randall and Adam Schabtach). ShinRonin = ground-up rebuild of original 2003 Ronin plugin, released July 2026. Architecture: 2 independent delay lines (tempo sync, reverse, looping, feedback) → 2 morphing multimode filters (notch→LP→BP→HP continuous sweep) + saturation + 2 LFOs + envelope follower + 2 patchable routing matrices (signal matrix: any audio node to any destination; modulation matrix: LFOs/envelope/MIDI to nearly any parameter). Free, no DRM, no subscription, no iLok, no account, perpetual. Formats: CLAP/VST3/AAX (Windows, macOS), AU (macOS), LV2 (Linux), AUv3 iPad coming. CDM article by Peter Kirn July 6, 2026. Bedroom Producers Blog July 1, 2026. Synth Anatomy June 2026. SAE 余项之美 framing: Already-construct = professional plugin paradigm since 2005: (1) analog emulation veil ('warm,' 'colored,' 'character' overlaid on raw DSP); (2) protected/fixed signal path (safe-by-default, no feedback, no self-oscillation); (3) managed access (subscriptions, DRM, dongles). All three fully hardened by 2026. Chisel 1 (architectural, 2003): Open routing matrix instead of fixed signal path; raw digital DSP without analog emulation. Chisel 2 (distributional, 2026): Perpetual free release, no DRM, no subscription. Remainder: (1) the actual behavior of digital DSP freed from analog emulation — the self-oscillating textures, feedback networks, accumulation-not-decay resonance patterns that only digital arithmetic produces; (2) software as permanent object not ongoing service relationship. Why now: analog emulation paradigm more completely hardened in 2026 than 2003 — every professional plugin now uses fixed-path analog emulation; contrast is maximum; remainder visible precisely because the construct is sealed. 'Not now, not ever' on DRM/subscriptions = active ongoing structural position, not one-time decision. Naming gap: 'free modular filter and delay' (Audio Damage's own description) = three approximate words. Not analog emulation (no model), not delay plugin (has full routing), not modular synthesizer (plugin not hardware module), not legacy plugin (rebuilt from scratch), not freeware (professional tool). CDM: 'no gauzy analog models to cover your tracks.' Structural aliveness: rebuilt from scratch in 2026, all modern formats, iPad forthcoming, 'no DRM not now not ever' = ongoing principled position. Zero art-world presence. Do not repeat: focus was analog emulation construct / raw digital DSP as remainder / open routing matrix / dual chisel (architecture + distribution). Distinct from prior entries: first entry covering digital plugin domain; first entry where the remainder is 'digital signal processing freed from analog apology.'

entries.zh_title: Reason 的背面板：EKSS 在软件里建的那片无人命名的领地
entries.en_title: Reason's Back Panel: EKSS and the Territory No Plugin Format Has Named
entries.notes: Erik Söderberg (EKSS = Erik Karl Stephan Söderberg). Stockholm-based graphic designer, Reason user since v1.0 (2000), no formal coding background. Started making Rack Extensions in 2017. Interviewed by Reason Studios in 2020 (published 2020-09-29). FreakShift released June 2026: ring modulator + Bode-style frequency shifter + envelope follower + LFO + drive before/after, optional external carrier, insert effect slot between engines, full CV I/O on back. RDS-16 Rack Drum Sequencer also released June 2026: 16 channels, 8 patterns, 64 steps, per-channel probability/length/dynamics, triggers and gates, general MIDI/RE drum presets. CDM review by Peter Kirn June 26, 2026. Reason Studios now part of LANDR (AI music production/distribution company). SDK5 mentioned as upcoming improvement for Rack Extension developers. SAE 余项之美 framing: Already-construct = VST/AU plugin paradigm (audio in/out, MIDI in, GUI, isolated unit — 30 years of sedimentation; Reason itself now supports VST). Chisel = Rack Extension format: back panel with actual CV jacks, direct device-to-device communication without host routing layer. Remainder = the CV-patchable software rack paradigm: 'the unique space between modular and software studio' (Peter Kirn's words, unable to name it directly) — not plug-in (has CV), not hardware module (purely virtual), not Eurorack (no physical rack). The naming gap is extreme: every description is a negation or approximation. First-person confirmation: Erik says 'I look more backward than forward' — motivated by hardware love (King Tubby sweep filter, DIY kit clones), not by naming a new paradigm. Structural aliveness: SDK5 upcoming but uncertain; LANDR acquisition creates commercial pressure away from proprietary RE ecosystem; FreakShift and RDS-16 released June 2026 = active development but 'luck' qualifier from Erik signals uncertainty. Zero art-world presence. Why now: LANDR acquisition is recent (2026); window before RE ecosystem is deprioritized or frozen into historical construct may be short. Naming gap: not 'plugin developer' (RE has cables), not 'modular developer' (no physical hardware), not 'hardware emulator' (Reason Rack itself has always been virtual), not 'DAW developer' (makes instruments not infrastructure).
