entries.project_name: Magnus Lidström (Sonic Charge) / PhenoType for Synplant 2
entries.zh_title: PhenoType：那部从未被写下的合成器词典
entries.en_title: PhenoType: The Synthesizer's Unwritten Dictionary
entries.notes: Magnus Lidström (NuEdge Development / Sonic Charge), Swedish developer based in Sweden. Sonic Charge products: Synplant 2 (€149, organic genetic synthesizer), Microtonic (drum synthesizer), Permut8 (bit manipulation effect), Bitspeek (speech vocoder), ChordBud 2 (MIDI chord generator). PhenoType: free extension for Synplant 2 users, released June 2026. Requires Synplant 2 license (not free version). Runs as JavaScript engine inside Synplant 2 plugin — no internet, no cloud, no tokens, fully local. Interface: single text input field + EXE button + RND button. Type description → generates fully editable Synplant 2 patch in 2-3 seconds. Generated patch can be further mutated/branched in Synplant's gene editor. CDM article by Peter Kirn, June 10, 2026. Synth Anatomy review June 10, 2026. GearNews article June 2026. Development backstory: Magnus started by building an algorithm to automatically describe Synplant patches using words and tags — 'at some point we started thinking: if an algorithm can create descriptions from patches, should it not also be possible to run the process in reverse?' Self-labeled 60,000 patches by hand (Magnus himself: 'yep, all by myself hehe'). ~200 internal tags, ~1,000 synonyms+variations+misspellings. Understands simple inversions ('without reverb,' 'not distorted'). RND button generates randomized prompts (all meaningful, not nonsensical — the vocabulary is constrained). Known gaps: music genres, exotic instruments (Magnus: 'But we will get there in time'). SAE 余项之美 framing: Already-construct 1 = Synplant's 20-year genetic/prelinguistic interface paradigm — knob names chiseled, parameter labels chiseled, sound categories chiseled; language stays out by design; this IS the Synplant already-construct, hardened over 20+ years of users and presets. Already-construct 2 = 'AI audio = large cloud model + massive dataset + text prompt → audio output' — Suno, Udio, Stable Audio, ElevenLabs; all assume bigness, cloudness, opacity. Double chisel: PhenoType chisels construct 1 by granting language access to the genetic space; chisels construct 2 by removing everything big — one person, one synthesizer, local model, no cloud. Double remainder: (1) The phenotypic space of Synplant 2 — the full semantic map of timbral possibilities, which was always latent in the parameter space but never surfaced in language; (2) The small-local-instrument-specific model path for AI-assisted sound — which was always structurally possible but is being absorbed by the large-model paradigm. Biological name significance: 'phenotype' = observable expression of genotype. Magnus chose a genetics term, not a software category term, because the software category doesn't exist yet. Why now: 'AI audio = large model' construct is closing all imagination space for what neural networks can do with sound; the small/local/instrument-specific path becomes a historical footnote once that equation seals. Vocabulary still growing (June 2026 = v1.0, acknowledged gaps). Naming gap: not AI generation (no big model), not preset browser (generates new patches), not randomizer (directional semantic bias), not text-to-audio (returns editable parameters, not audio), not chatbot (no conversation). No art-world presence. Logic actively growing — vocabulary gaps acknowledged, further development implied. Note: no image downloaded (proxy restricted).

entries.zh_title: 引力：钟摆不知道它在演奏
entries.en_title: Gravity: The Pendulum Doesn't Know It's Playing
entries.notes: Stuart Frederich-Smith (shotsy), Portland-based, runs SignalFunctionSet. Free open-source VCV Rack modules, EYESY video synth modes, SampleStack sample manager, workshops with Synth Library Portland. Prior archaeological ports: Barry Truax's GSX (1985), Steve Reich tape phasing, Paul DeMarinis' Pygmy Gamelan, IRCAM CHANT. Gravity: released May 15, 2026. 30HP VCV Rack module. Six modes: (1) Pendulum = double pendulum RK4; (2) Gravity Well = rocket in planetary gravity; (3) Billiards = elastic balls, cue ball tracked; (4) Hungry Man = Pac-Man-style polar maze; (5) Turtle = LOGO turtle with random drawing commands; (6) Pattern = Maurer rose r=sin((p/q)θ). Outputs: X/Y (±5V), RADIUS, ANGLE, SECTOR 1-6, GATE 1-6. CDM June 18, 2026, Peter Kirn. SAE 余项之美 framing: Already-construct = step sequencer note-list paradigm (all modular sequencers + chaos/random modules still work within it). Chisel = remove note list; use physical system spatial trajectory as voltage source. Remainder = spatial trajectories of physical systems (pendulum arc, billiard reflections, turtle paths, rose geometry, orbital perturbations) — always potentially musical but never absorbed into sequencer paradigm. Not random (deterministic), not designed (initial conditions not outcomes), not AI generative. Third state: determined-but-not-commandable geometry. Second-order: Frederich-Smith's archaeological practice — recovering historical computer music from sediment. Naming gap: not 'sequencer' (no note list), not 'chaos module' (not electrical feedback), not 'random source' (deterministic), not 'LFO' (not periodic). Creator's own label 'chaos and motion engine' = approximation, both words slightly wrong. No image (proxy). Zero art-world presence. Logic growing — more modules in pipeline, MetaModule Eurorack ports ongoing.

entries.zh_title: 声音地形学：Incline 把时间轴从颗粒合成里拿走之后
entries.en_title: Sonic Topography: What Incline Found When It Removed the Time Axis
entries.notes: Cristián Vogel, Scottish-born electronic musician, long career in techno and experimental electronics. NeverEngineLabs (NEL) = his software/instrument development operation. Also makes WaveKitchen (wavetable generation studio). Incline: 'Toposonic Corpus Explorer' — analysis-driven granular instrument. Released March 2026 on macOS, Easter update April 5 2026 (echo, display improvements, output quality). Windows version not yet released but flagged as coming (per user requests). Price: €30 (sale from €55), 7-day free trial available. Standalone app, not a plugin. CDM article by Peter Kirn, March 30, 2026. Synth Anatomy article March 2026. KVR Audio forum thread. Technical: uses ML segmentation algorithms to analyze audio corpus, arranges grains by perceptual similarity in 2D space (not time axis). Three modes: One Shot (direct segment audition, ratchet playback), One Loop (continuous traversal, micro-loop continuity), Cloud (distributed granular scheduling, evolving textures). All modes: Contour Sequencer (autonomous traversal along topographic contour lines, timing synchronization). Full wavetable envelope engine (Hanning, Gaussian, plus 140 factory wavetables + WaveKitchen import). MIDI learn available. SAE 余项之美 framing: Already-construct = granular synthesis time-axis paradigm (Xenakis → Gabor → Roads, 70 years unquestioned; ALL granular tools — Granulator II, Sampler, Borderlands — operate within same coordinate system). Chisel = remove time axis from definition; replace with sonic content topology via ML perceptual similarity. Remainder = the topological content relationships between grains — how they cluster, differ, what paths connect them — always latent in every audio file but never accessed because time axis was always there first. Two closure threats: (1) 'AI audio = prompt → output' consolidating, sonic topology becoming sealed infrastructure; (2) academic corpus synthesis naming (FluCoMa = audio descriptor navigation by descriptor, different epistemology; descriptor navigation ≠ content topology). Naming gap: not granular synthesis (Peter Kirn hesitates to use the term); not AI generation (no prompts, you navigate); not sampler (not sequential playback); not corpus-based synthesis in FluCoMa sense (FluCoMa navigates by audio descriptors/analysis, not by learned content topology from ML segmentation — different logic). Creator's own term 'toposonic corpus explorer' = empty set, Incline only member. Zero art-world presence. Logic actively growing — Windows version pending, ongoing development. Note: no image downloaded (proxy restricted).

entries.zh_title: 两根触摸条：Flexur 找回键盘凿掉的那段路
entries.en_title: Sound Workshop Flexur: The Path Between Notes the Keyboard Erased
entries.notes: Sound Workshop: one-person instrument design operation run by Chris (no last name found in public sources). Previously shipped Wiggler (expressive synth), Quord (harmonic drone synth, 35 units shipped), 550 LinnStrument overlay surfaces. Flexur T2: Trautonium-inspired standalone expressive synthesizer. Preorder opened June 2026: $1,399 (presale), $1,599 (final). Sold out 135 units in 5 days, raised $186,000. Ships 6-24 months from June 2026. Specs: 450×280×70mm, two floating touch bars (15mm semitone pitch, 23 semitones), knob-per-function subtractive synth, 6×12 mod matrix, preset/autotune/mono/poly/arp, USB-C MIDI out, TRS MIDI in/out with MPE, 4x CV out (pitch/gate/push/envelope), 2x expression/gate in, full-size balanced instrument jacks. Four working prototypes tested with 100+ users. Building first 100 units in-house. CDM article by Peter Kirn June 24, 2026; Synthtopia June 9, 2026; Synth Anatomy June 8, 2026. Trautonium background: Friedrich Trautwein + Oskar Sala, Berlin 1930s. Metal wire on resistance rail = continuous pitch. Sala used for 40 years: 'The Birds' bird sounds (Hitchcock, 1963), experimental works mostly unreleased. Sala died 2002. Jürgen Hiller (Trautoniks) continues Trautonium tradition. Moog Subharmonicon (2020) is Trautonium-inspired but focuses on subharmonic synthesis, not touch bar interface. SAE 余项之美 framing: Already-construct = piano keyboard discrete pitch grid (3 centuries → analog synthesis → MIDI → DAW timeline → MPE). MPE is latest construct extension: each key gets pitch bend + pressure, but starting point remains fixed-pitch discrete grid. Chisel = floating touch bar replaces keyboard starting point entirely: continuous pitch space is the default, stable notes are the arrival, glide is not decorative but structural. Remainder #1 = continuous pitch space between notes (the glide, the bend, the vibrato, the singer's path) — never physically gone, declared unplayable by keyboard structure, minimally served by pitch-bend wheel. Remainder #2 = coupling of pitch and dynamics in same gesture (voice's natural state) — keyboard severs this: velocity = attack only, finger pressure post-attack disconnected from sound. Touch bar: pressing harder throughout note = live control of filter/volume, always coupled to pitch position, restoring voice-like coupling. Chris's own words: 'Our mission is to make an instrument that allows me to play the vocal melodies from my favorite songs. When people sing, they constantly flip back and forth between jumps and slides. The Trautonium bars allow you to do both.' Why now: MPE hardening into 'expressive synthesis' construct (Haken Continuum, ROLI, LinnStrument all use MPE). Once 'expressive synthesis = extended keyboard + MPE' names the space, touch-bar continuous-pitch alternative becomes historical footnote. Flexur exists before naming closes. Naming gap extreme: not theremin (electromagnetic field, no physical contact with bar), not ribbon controller (controller not generator; no push-dynamics coupling), not Ondes Martenot (has a keyboard you slide; keyboard-derived), not MPE synthesizer (MPE extends keyboard), not 'expressive synthesizer' (category claimed by MPE instruments). Trautonium-inspired = category of exactly two historical members. No art-world presence. Logic still growing: first customer ship pending, Patreon updates monthly, design iteration ongoing. Note: no image downloaded (proxy restricted).

entries.zh_title: Jim Sachs：为无人注视的时刻造了一个水族馆
entries.en_title: Jim Sachs Built an Aquarium for the Moments Nobody Is Watching
entries.notes: Jim Sachs, computer artist, US Air Force C-141 Starlifter pilot background. Known for Amiga Lagoon (iconic image for Brilliance paint software), game art for Defender of the Crown and Ports of Call. SereneScreen: his software house. Marine Aquarium: virtual aquarium screensaver, 30+ years of iteration, available on Windows/macOS/iOS/Android. Android 10 version released June 2026. Appeared in Smallville, Law & Order, Bridget Jones Diary, reportedly at Cannes. Microsoft bundled into Windows XP Plus! Pack. CDM article by Peter Kirn, June 29, 2026. SAE 余项之美 framing: Already-construct = screen as attentional instrument (every pixel must serve a task/notification/content; Screen Time tracking quantifies and rations all viewing); After Dark / screensaver format evolved from CRT burn-in protection tool into a medium for contemplative imagery. Chisel = occupy the time that falls entirely outside attention: screensaver activates when the human departs, deactivates when they return. Remainder = the interval between two moments of attention — the gap that no productivity discourse can claim, no Screen Time metric can count, because it runs for no one. Sachs built a 30-year practice inside this gap. Why now: LCD/OLED eliminates burn-in need; smartphones kill the blank-screen concept (always-on displays, lock screen content); Apple restricts screensaver function on iOS (run in fullscreen only); ambient computing fills the gap with notifications. The specific temporal interval the screensaver once occupied is being abolished. Sachs continues updating without accepting retro/nostalgia framing. Naming gap: not pixel art (Direct3D fish), not digital art (no galleries), not game art (screensaver not game), not screensaver developer (Cannes/Bridget Jones). Most accurate description = images that run when nobody is watching — no existing name. Art world slowly approaching via digital folklore, ambient computing aesthetics, beauty-of-useful-objects discourse, but Sachs himself not named/categorized there. No image downloaded (proxy blocked). Zero art-world presence. Logic still growing — new platform versions in 2026.

entries.zh_title: Noisferatu：当比特运算开口说话
entries.en_title: Noisferatu: When Bit Arithmetic Starts to Speak
entries.notes: Robert Heel (scaepe), Berlin. Noisferatu: compact handheld generative texture synthesizer. 45 algorithms across 5 banks: (1) Wavetables — glitchy bursts, evolving soundscapes; (2) Noisy Textures — noise/dust/rhythmic grain; (3) BitBend — wavetable address manipulation (bit shifts, XOR, truncation, offset injection on the lookup index itself); (4) Blips & Tones — most tonal bank; (5) Logic Disorder — two oscillators processed through bitwise logic operations (XOR, AND, OR at binary signal level). Hardware: Seeed Studio XIAO SAMD21 microcontroller, 5 potentiometers, 3 buttons, LED display, audio output, USB-C power. Firmware and schematics open source on GitHub (rob-scape/noisferatu). DIY kit from Thonk (£69). Front/back panel reversible (show or hide Nosferatu graphic). CDM article by Peter Kirn, June 23, 2026. Also covered by Synthtopia (June 25, 2026), Synth Anatomy, Matrixsynth. SAE 余项之美 framing: Already-construct = invisible computational substrate in digital audio — GUI hides DSP code, presets hide algorithms, AI audio generation completes the chain (describe → output, full computational opacity). Wavetable synthesis already-construct = address is purely instrumental, never aesthetic. Chisel: BitBend bends the address calculation itself (the index used to look up sample values); Logic Disorder applies bit-level boolean operations (XOR/AND/OR) to oscillator outputs at the binary signal encoding layer. Remainder: (1) The addressing arithmetic of wavetable lookup — normally sealed infrastructure, now the sound generator; (2) The bitwise logic relationship between two digital signals — which every DAW/synthesizer has always suppressed, now the aesthetic substance; (3) The DSP implementation layer more broadly (the C code), which AI audio makes maximally invisible but Noisferatu makes directly playable. Translation guide in manual (Max gen~ / VCV Rack → Noisferatu C code) makes DSP code a playable instrument paradigm. Naming gap: not glitch art (aesthetic of errors, not of substrate), not circuit bending (hardware modification), not bitcrushing (quantization depth reduction), not wavetable synthesis (address is still instrumental there), not noise machine (has algorithmic structure). 'Computational substrate synthesis' — the method of making DSP implementation layers themselves audible — has no existing name. GitHub open for contributions, each new algorithm asks: what other implementation layers can speak? Zero art-world presence. Logic actively growing.

entries.zh_title: 潜在地形：当编解码器的内部空间变得可演奏
entries.en_title: Latent Terrain: When the Codec's Interior Becomes an Instrument
entries.notes: Jasper Shuoyang Zheng (Shuoyang Jasper Zheng), PhD student at Queen Mary University of London, UKRI CDT in Artificial Intelligence and Music, supervised by Anna Xambó Sedó and Nick Bryan-Kinns. Latent Terrain (nn.terrain~ Max external package): open-source tool for building corpus-based sound spaces by navigating the latent space of neural audio codecs. Developed over 12 months through performance practice + collaboration with 4 musicians. Displayed at Sónar+D 2025 and NIME 2026 London. CDM article by Peter Kirn, June 17, 2026. Supported codecs: RAVE (ACIDS-IRCAM, Antoine Caillon & Philippe Esling), Music2Latent-Scripted (Marco Pasini, Stefan Lattner, George Fazekas / Sony CSL), Stable Audio Open 1.0 autoencoder (pretransform only, not diffusion model), SAME-S (Stable Audio 3 autoencoder). Four collaborators: Keigo Yoshida (EEG→terrain, adversarial calm/arousal tension), Jiatong Liu (Beijing Hutong archival recordings → spatial ambient archive, nn/mémoire), Nico García-Peguinho (active listening as compositional approach), Dan Hearn (explorative and serendipitous workflow). Technical: builds a coordinates-to-latents supervised ML model; trains on pairs of spatial trajectories and latent trajectories; terrain = surface map for codec latent space; navigate with mouse/stylus/sensor/controller; navigate slowly = gradual timbral shifts; fast = fracture, jump, develop texture. SAE 余项之美 framing: Already-construct = neural audio codec as compression infrastructure — all AI audio generation treats latent space as means not destination; even experimental real-time RAVE performance moves through latent space from A to B, never inhabits it; codec builds internal timbral topology as byproduct of efficient compression, never intended as creative space. Chisel = suspend codec's purpose entirely; ask what shape the learned space is; expose the never-meant-to-be-traversed interior geometry as navigable instrument. Remainder = codec's learned timbral topology (how sounds relate, cluster, transition) which was always there but was never the point; the organizing logic of the codec's understanding of sound, now playable. Why now: 'AI audio = prompt → generation' construct is solidifying, closing the imagination space for inhabiting codec interiors before it's fully named; NIME 2026 = beginning of academic naming but not complete; Max for Live devices inbound, codec support expanding, PD version being considered. Naming gap: not AI generation (no prompts), not synthesizer (no oscillators), not sampler (structural geometry not audio material), not FluCoMa (FluCoMa uses audio analysis descriptors; Latent Terrain uses learned latent topology — different epistemologies). Creator's own words: 'I'm not particularly interested in typing prompts to make stuff, I'm interested in breaking them and dissecting them, and when you crack them open, what's inside turns out to be genuinely playable.' PhD dissertation title: 'Discovering Musical Affordances in Neural Audio Synthesis.' Image downloaded from GitHub (open-graphic.jpg). Zero art-world presence. Logic actively growing.

entries.zh_title: Glosso：说不出字的那张嘴
entries.en_title: Glosso: A Mouth That Cannot Form Words
entries.notes: Jelle Akkerman (jellea on GitHub/X), engineer and artist based in Northern Italy. Opened for the Vengaboys at age 14 at the local zoo. every something = his creative imprint for music, hardware, software. Also makes Eurorack modules (polytemporal-instruments.com) with Dr. Nicolas Bougaïeff and Johannes Lohbihler (dadamachines / tbd 16). Glosso: instrument plugin (generator, no input required), €25 / free trial (10 min/day). Artikulation: polyrhythmic groove manipulator effect plugin, €25. perp (Risset rhythm live looper) and otophon (psychoacoustic tone generator) coming July 2026. CDM article by Peter Kirn, June 3, 2026. SAE 余项之美 framing: Already-construct = vocal synthesis as directed utterance (Klatt 1980s → Vocaloid → neural TTS) — entire lineage is history of making machines say what you want. Chisel = Hordijk's rungler logic: two oscillators coupled through shift register in feedback loop, each feeding the other, producing pseudorandom behavior neither random nor commandable. Jelle runs two rungler-style circuits through vowel formant filters. Remainder = phonemic form after semantic control is removed: vowel contours and consonantal rhythms roam freely without a directing intention. This is structurally glossolalia (speaking in tongues): the remainder of language-form after meaning is removed. Second-order: Hordijk died 2019; Benjolin entering historicization phase (commercial clones, museum pieces, masterclasses). Rungler logic shifting from 'living structural method' to 'Hordijk's named technique.' Glosso catches it before hardening completes, moves it into vocal formant space it has never inhabited. Naming gap: not vocal synth (can't direct phonemes), not noise (has phonemic structure), not formant filter (generates), not granular (circuit-based time structure), not random (internal consistency). Site description: 'your computer speaks in tongues' — name is experience, not category. Logic still growing (2 more plugins July 2026). Zero art-world presence.

entries.zh_title: Dither：凿掉基底之后，素描本身剩了下来
entries.en_title: Dither: When You Chisel Away the Substrate, the Sketch Remains
entries.notes: Lingdong Huang, PhD student in Future Sketches group at MIT Media Lab (Zach Lieberman). Dither: WIP creative coding language released August 2025 (v0.0.1), v0.0.2 November 2025, v0.0.3 April 2026 (Mac IDE, 8MB, bundles VM/compiler/REPL/debugger/stdlib/docs). GitHub: LingDong-/dither-lang, 50 stars. Featured on CAN October 16, 2025. Presented as poster at Media Lab Scalable HCI Symposium 2026. Key capability: same Dither code runs on CPU or GPU, web or native — one source, all substrates. Type inference (no manual vec3 declarations), built-in vector/matrix math, pixel-focused stdlib. SAE 余项之美 framing: Already-construct = CPU/GPU bifurcation in creative coding (Processing/p5.js vs GLSL/WGSL), hardened over 20+ years into separate communities, learning curves, and epistemologies that cannot communicate. Chisel = treating substrate as a backend detail. Remainder = the creative coding practice itself — intuition-to-pixel — which never needed substrate knowledge but was forced to carry it for two decades. Second-order remainder / name-as-program: 'dithering' in image processing = distributing quantization error spatially to simulate tones beyond hardware limit. The language's name encodes its own operation: it redistributes the creative potential that fell into the CPU/GPU gap. Name is a remainder-operation, not a metaphor. Naming gap: not Processing (not Java/browser-only legacy), not p5.js (not browser-only, compiles to GPU/native), not GLSL/WGSL (has type inference, control flow, high-level abstractions), not game engine scripting (no game constructs), not esolang (actually productive). Huang's other projects: drawing language from lambda calculus, version control for visual sketches, gestural computation experiment — all investigate the gap between creative intuition and coding tools. Logic still growing: v0.0.3 still pre-release, 1 open issue asking how GPU backend works. Zero art-world presence.

entries.project_name: Fernando G. Tamajon (AudioWanderer) / AW Noise Maker
entries.zh_title: 那台学不会的机器
entries.en_title: The Machine You Cannot Learn
entries.notes: Fernando G. Tamajon (b.1978 Málaga), audiovisual artist active as AudioWanderer and MALAVENTURA in southern Spain since 2000. Twenty years of experimental generative music tools (Lemur, Lua, Arduino) freely shared online. AW Noise Maker: first hardware device, handmade, small run, sold via audiowanderer.com. Sneak preview on Synthtopia May 10, 2026; CDM review by Peter Kirn June 10, 2026. Hardware: OLED display (shows glitch patterns unrelated to any parameter), 4 controls (2 buttons, 2 knobs), USB-C power, stereo minijack output, random FX reinitialize every boot. Design ethos: 'a non-idiomatic synth made not to be controlled or understood in any manner' (handwritten warning in box). SAE 余项之美 framing: Already-construct = synthesizer's implicit promise of learnability: even 'chaos synths' (Rungler, Lyra-8, Strega) reward invested attention; time in, control gained. Chisel = Noise Maker removes learnability as design goal entirely: random FX on every boot breaks feedback loop of learning; OLED glitch pattern gives no parameter feedback; no documentation; no preset memory. Remainder = 'surfable wave' (Peter Kirn's phrase): playability that emerges AFTER all paths to understanding are removed; state-reading rather than parameter-mapping. Second-order remainder: inversion of 20 years of generative practice — the remainder of a career of making shareable tools is a device designed to be neither shareable nor comprehensible. Naming gap: 'non-idiomatic synth' borrows from Derek Bailey's 'non-idiomatic improvisation' but applies it to hardware design — a device not within any synthesis paradigm. Not 'noise machine' (understood to make noise), not 'chaos synth' (rewards learning), not 'broken instrument' (intentional), not 'generative music' (no generative system). AI contrast: AI's unexpectedness = surprise from inside a training set (within expectation); Noise Maker's = removal of expectation entirely. Two different kinds of remainder, two different relationships to the unknown — distinction not yet named. Zero art-world presence. Logic still growing — first hardware from a software/generative practice, structural implications still unfolding.

entries.zh_title: Sphere Paint：凿去边缘之后，剩下的那种绘画
entries.en_title: Sphere Paint: What Painting Looks Like After the Edge Is Gone
entries.notes: Grant Custer, designer-programmer at The Browser Company. Constraint Systems: an ongoing collection of 46+ browser-based 'alternative interfaces for editing and creating images and text' (GitHub: constraint-systems). Sphere Paint released May 21, 2026. URL: sphere-paint.constraint.systems. Browser-based multiplayer painting on a sphere surface. No edges, no orientation, no up/down/left/right. All points geometrically equivalent. You can only paint while zoomed in — never see the whole. No undo; erasing = painting over with white. Custer's own words: 'A sphere surface is interesting because all points are continuous on all sides. You can respond, extend, or connect in any direction. I'm interested to see if certain drawings might become landmarks or growing territories over time. The dynamic where you can only draw zoomed in is a play on the fact that we can only act locally, in small patches of a larger world. I kept the feature set small... I'm interested in site-spaces that feel solid, self-contained, and strange.' SAE 余项之美 framing: Already-construct = rectangular canvas (encodes: edges, center/margin hierarchy, reading direction, God's-eye zoom-out). Chisel = Sphere Paint removes edge entirely — sphere topology has no boundary, no privileged vantage point. Remainder = (1) image-making logic that emerges when compositional habit has no edge to push against: marks sediment instead of compose; 'landmarks' and 'territories' emerge from sphere topology not human composition; (2) no-undo makes sphere a geological record of time rather than carrier of intention; (3) no God's-eye view — collaboration on an object you can never fully see simultaneously. Second-order remainder: csOS (constraint-systems 'OS' using iframes, updated May 21 2026) lets users chain multiple constraint tools into custom creative pipelines — the final image is the remainder of a chain of remainders. Naming gap: not collaborative design tool (no layers/structure/purpose), not game (no win condition), not social platform (no profiles/feeds), not generative art (requires human action), not VR art (browser, no headset), not 360° video (painting not photography). Custer's own term 'site-spaces that feel solid, self-contained, and strange' = self-evidently still being invented. Constraint Systems recently featured in Slanted Magazine (June 4, 2026 feed post). Also on mod-lab.org. GitHub: 89 followers, csOS updated May 21 2026. sphere-paint repo still marked WIP. Logic still growing: sphere-draw WIP, cosine (text embedding tool) updated Feb 2026. Zero art-world presence. Do not repeat: focus was rectangle-as-construct / sphere-topology-as-remainder / geological-sediment-not-composition angle. Distinct from all prior entries: first entry covering browser-based collaborative canvas / topology-as-constraint.

entries.zh_title: Prāsa：泰卢固格律里藏着的那台机器
entries.en_title: Prāsa: The Machine Hidden Inside Telugu Meter
entries.notes: Koundinya Dhulipalla, artist-developer based in London. Prāsa: an esoteric programming language built on Telugu chandassu (classical poetic meter). Code organized into cells (4-space indent = move 1 cell forward on Turing Machine tape). Cell values = syllable counts of each line. Bracket scaling: syllables within () are multiplied into cell's existing value. Validity constraint: cumulative syllabic stress pattern (U=stressed, I=unstressed) must match one of four classical Telugu meters: Utpalamāla (UII UIU III UII UII UIU IU, 20 syl), Campakamāla (III IUI UII IUI IUI IUI UIU, 21 syl), Mattēbham (IIU UII UIU III UUU IUU IU, 20 syl), Śārdūlam (UUU IIU IUI IIU UUI UUI U, 19 syl). Uses CMU English pronunciation dictionary for syllabification. GitHub: github.com/koundinyad/prasa-language. Browser editor at prasa.software/write. Research documentation at poetic.computer. Published paper: 'Vernacular computing as encoded aesthetics for decolonial code intervention' in AI & Society (Springer, 2025), vol. 41:2683-2695. Featured in EsoNatLangs article on esoteric.codes, April 16, 2026. SAE 余项之美 framing: Already-construct = Western programming formalism (ALGOL blocks, Boolean logic, lambda calculus, indentation-as-structure) — all derived from Western math/logic traditions, entirely deaf to the sonic/prosodic dimension of language. Chisel = Prāsa strips away Western syntactic logic while keeping surface features (indentation, text), but makes syllabic stress the actual computational constraint and tape-movement the spatial model. Remainder = Telugu chandassu, a 2000-year-old formal system for encoding patterns in time (laghuvu/guruvu stress sequences), which is structurally analogous to computation but was never absorbed into programming. Sanskrit chandas (parent tradition) was essentially a rule-governed formal grammar for symbol sequences — functionally the same kind of thing as a programming language — but when computing formed in the West, it drew only from Western traditions. Chandassu became remainder. Prāsa proves it never disappeared. Second-order remainder: the sonic/oral dimension of code — the fact that code sounds like something when read aloud — which all PLs have always discarded. Naming gap: not a programming language (not for practical use), not code poetry (actually runs), not decolonial theory (working tool), not music (uses English phonetics not Telugu sounds), not Telugu language learning (CMU dictionary, English words). Naming attempt in progress: 'vernacular computing' (Dhulipalla 2025 paper) and 'EsoNatLang' (esoteric.codes April 2026) are the first clustering attempts. Zero art-world presence. Logic actively growing.

entries.zh_title: Rejoice：凿掉位置之后，袋中剩余的那些

entries.notes: Rejoice by Devine Lu Linvega (Hundred Rabbits), released April 2026. A concatenative programming language where the entire program state is a multiset (unordered bag of symbols), and all operations are fractions: denominator = remove from bag, numerator = add to bag. Built in Uxntal, running on the Uxn VM. Documentation written in Peano's Latino Sine Flexione. Key SAE 余项之美 framing: (1) Already-construct = stack-based concatenative computation (Forth lineage) where position is the foundation of meaning; (2) Chisel = removal of position entirely — only kind and quantity remain; (3) Remainder is literal: every fraction fires by subtracting its denominator from the bag, and the mathematical remainder in the bag IS the program state and output; (4) Second-order remainder: logic (NOT/AND/OR gates) emerges from fraction arithmetic, inverting the usual logic→arithmetic dependency hierarchy; (5) Documentation language enacts same chisel — Latino Sine Flexione strips Latin grammar the same way Rejoice strips positional computation; (6) Naming gap: 'Think Fractran without rule-searching, or Forth without a stack' — creator's own negating definition; not a multiset rewriting system (sequential, not parallel), not logic programming (no unification), not functional (no closures); (7) Structural aliveness: creator called it 'cursed idea,' opened Rewriting Mailinglist, connections to Interaction Nets/Pocket Nets/tropical arithmetic still being explored. entries.notes: Lyra Rebane (rebane2001), Estonia-based security researcher at RangeForce. 9 CVEs in Chrome. Former Cohoster. Speaker at Smashing Conf Meets Style Sheets (May 6, 2026), CSS Day 2026 (Amsterdam, June 11-12), BSides Tallinn 2024 & 2025, 39C3 (December 2025). Smashing Magazine Person of the Week (April 6, 2026). Philosophy: 'the best way to understand a system is to push it until it breaks—and then build something beautiful with the pieces.' 'computers are made for art and fun.' Does NOT use AI. x86CSS: working CSS-only x86 CPU emulator, published February 2026. 842 GitHub stars, 19 forks, 10 commits, 3 contributors, GPL-3.0. Handwritten CSS in Sublime Text, Python build script (build_css.py) for repetitive parts. Uses CSS features: if() statements, style queries, custom @functions, @property, container style queries, animation keyframes. CSS clock implementation: animation + style container queries (zero user input needed). Optional JS clock for stability only. 0x600 bytes (1.5kB) default memory, programs loaded at 0x100. Implements most 8086 instruction set. Can compile and run C programs via gcc-ia16. Preinstalled programs: Fibonacci sequence, Pascal's triangle, Wordle variant. Built on Jane Ori's 'CPU Hack' concept but goes far beyond — Ori's required hover interaction, Rebane's runs autonomously. Cohost shut down late 2024. CSS crimes community is remainder of Cohost's collapse. Triple chisel-construct cycle: (1) Web's tripartite separation (HTML=structure, CSS=presentation, JS=behavior) is fundamental construct of web dev since late 1990s. x86CSS chisels this by implementing arbitrary computation inside presentation layer. Remainder = CSS's accidental Turing-completeness, emerging from convergence of features each designed for styling purposes. No single feature was meant to compute; their combination produces universal computation as unintended product. (2) x86 CPU is construct of physical engineering — transistors, silicon, lithography, clock signals. x86CSS chisels away all materiality. Each instruction = cascade of custom property evaluations and style inheritance. CPU clock = animation keyframe. Memory = nested containers with style queries. Remainder = processor existing entirely as declarative rules. (3) Cohost's community construct (social platform where CSS was medium of expression) was destroyed when platform shut down. CSS crimes practice survived as remainder — skills acquired in dead community continue producing work after community's death. x86CSS is literally built with Cohost-era CSS skills. entries.zh_title: garden.ooo：当完成概念松动，网重新成为网
entries.en_title: garden.ooo: When the Concept of Completion Loosens, the Web Becomes a Web Again
entries.notes: Baku Hashimoto (橋本麦), visual artist based in Tokyo. Musashino Art University (2011-2013), SFPC NYC (Fall 2016). Known for generative art, motion graphics, stop-motion, interactive design. Awards: Cannes Lions Bronze (2016), Ars Electronica (2019), Tokyo TDC Grand Prize (2025). Published: UIST '25 (Tweeq parameter GUI), SIGGRAPH Asia '21 (Glisp Lisp-based design tool). garden.ooo: Local-First wiki-based CMS, actively developed since ~2024, updated April 2026. Former name: Morion. URL is both system and service name. Powers baku89.com through dogfooding. Tech: RxDB, IndexedDB, MongoDB, File System Access API, FileSystemObserver, Obsidian-compatible Markdown + YAML frontmatter. Five design principles: (1) Don't believe in hierarchy or linearity — no post types, no categories, no tag trees; structure emerges from links only; pages and tags not distinguished. (2) Local-First — local text files are SSOT, cloud is mirror; 3-layer: Local File ↔ Local DB (RxDB/IndexedDB) ↔ Remote DB (MongoDB); no account needed to start. (3) Plain text as universal interface — editable in Notepad, Obsidian, Cursor, or sed; enables integration with any AI system. (4) Afford leaking (ダダ漏れ) — mix public essays and private memos; content maturity as phase transition: gas (fragments) → liquid (amorphous) → crystal (archive); four visibility levels: public/unlisted/protected/private; 'unlisted' prevents context collapse by requiring contextual navigation. (5) Right to foolishness (愚行権) — user can customize parser, server does minimal sanitization, CMS doesn't police messy pages. Intellectual lineage: Ted Nelson/Xanadu, Tim Berners-Lee's rhizomatic web vision, Zettelkasten/Luhmann, Umesao Tadao's Kyoto-style cards (1969), Cosense/Scrapbox (pages ≡ tags), Obsidian (local-first), Neocities/HTML Energy, Olia Lialina's Vernacular Web. Web critique: CMS hierarchized the web, blogs linearized it into timelines, microblogs/Twitter completed linearization and destroyed link-mesh imagination, decontextualized list views cause context collapse. Triple chisel-construct: (1) CMS hierarchy-construct chiseled, remainder = emergent link topology (original web mesh); (2) cloud-first construct chiseled, remainder = local plain text files (most primitive/durable digital vessel); (3) completion-binary construct chiseled, remainder = vast grey zone between published and unpublished where human thought actually lives. Hashimoto's own phrase: '完成概念をガバガバにする' (loosen the concept of completion) = core declaration of remainder aesthetics. Naming gap: not CMS (no hierarchy), not wiki (portfolio/diary/paid content), not SSG (dynamic sync/DB), not Obsidian (public web publishing), not blog (no timeline), not digital garden tool (replication, paid content, graduated visibility). Not yet publicly released as platform — still growing through dogfooding. Zero art-world presence for this infrastructure practice specifically.
