entries.zh_title: SDF Editor：当曲面只是距离函数的零点余项
entries.en_title: SDF Editor: When the Surface Is Just the Zero-Crossing Remainder of a Distance Function
entries.notes: Johan Holwerda, Dutch developer, built a WebGPU-based SDF editor for Reinder Nijhoff's RenderQueue experimental rendering platform. Published January 8, 2026 as a guest post on reindernijhoff.net. The editor runs entirely in the browser using WebGPU compute shaders. Supports 6 primitive shapes (sphere, box, torus, capsule, cylinder, cone), 3 blend operations (union, subtraction, intersection) with smooth blending radius, hierarchical scene graphs with groups. Rendering pipeline: (1) update primitive buffer, (2) space partitioning via counting sort assigning primitives to grid cells, (3) dirty mask detecting changed cells, (4) octree split finding surface-containing cells, (5) surface extraction via Marching Cubes (edit mode) or Surface Nets (view mode), (6) ambient occlusion via 1024-direction shadow maps (Fibonacci spiral distribution), (7) final rendering with TAA. Key technical decisions driven by constraint: Surface Nets vertices rendered as pixel-sized points rather than triangles because finding neighboring vertices in 2^32-cell space would require 4 billion entry lookup table — too large. Point cloud is the remainder of this memory constraint. TAA fills gaps between points by blending sub-pixel jittered frames. Depth testing uses atomic max with two-step approach because WebGPU lacks 64-bit atomics. Dirty mask system preserves unchanged geometry from previous frames — image is palimpsest of computations from different moments. Triple chisel-construct cycle: (1) polygon modeling = construct of 3D form; SDF chisels away explicit geometric representation, leaving mathematical distance as remainder — surface never stored, only implied by zero-crossing; (2) triangle rendering = construct of real-time graphics; memory constraints chisel away triangle indices, leaving isolated points as remainder; (3) WebGPU = remainder of browser security model chiseling away native GPU access. Naming gap: not CAD (no engineering constraints, no manufacturing export), not sculpting app (no brushes, no clay metaphor), not shader toy (has full scene graph with groups and booleans), not math visualizer (produces actual 3D objects), not game engine (no physics, no scripting). Five naming systems fail simultaneously. Lives on renderqueue.dev — Reinder Nijhoff's personal experimental platform (also creator of Turtletoy and Dittytoy). Guest contribution format: neither paper nor product, neither demo nor tool. Holwerda's TODO includes OBJ export, gallery, world-space transforms, multi-select — logic still growing. Limitations acknowledged: 512MB buffer fits ~44M points, overdraw on thin surfaces, slow large-object moves. Zero art-world presence.

entries.zh_title: Envion：当包络线成为所有声音的余项
entries.en_title: Envion: When the Envelope Becomes Every Sound's Remainder
entries.notes: Emiliano Pennisi (Avenir), Palermo-based sound artist active since 1990s, originally trained as graphic designer, self-taught in sound. Released on Opal Tapes, Concrete Records, Heat Crimes, Tiptop Audio. Hosts monthly show on LYL Radio. Curates Paradigma (Palermo expanded listening collective) and r/musiconcrete subreddit. Envion: algorithmic dynatext envelope sequencer built entirely in Pure Data / PlugData. 151 GitHub stars, 1117 commits, 6 forks, MIT license. Core concept: envelope-first composition — thousands of 'dynatext triplets' (amplitude, duration, offset) stored as text files, sent to vline~, each line = one temporal gesture. A sound fragment (even milliseconds) is multiplied into thousands of variants by these gestures. Sound demoted to carrier; temporal shape = the music. Net-Audio module fetches random sound from Internet Archive, Wikimedia Commons, Freesound — 'Found Net Sound' concept. IMPRINTAPE: convolution tape deck with real hardware impulse responses. DYNAGRAN: granular engine as 'articulator not effect.' Runs on macOS/Windows/iPadOS via PlugData. CDM feature by Peter Kirn Oct 2025. Triple chisel-construct: (1) sound design = electronic music construct, envelope = remainder; Envion chisels sound primacy, renders it arbitrary, leaves envelope as sole creative medium; (2) sampler construct = preserving sample identity; Envion chisels identity through envelope multiplication; (3) music production speed = DAW construct; Envion demands 'slowing down' and 'patient listening,' explicitly resists productivity. Pure Data itself is remainder of Max/MSP commercialization. Naming gap: not synthesizer, not sampler, not drum machine, not DAW, not live coding env, not granular synth, not manual musique concrète. Pennisi's name: 'Algorithmic Dynatext Envelope Sequencer' — no existing category. Influenced by Di Scipio, Roland Kayn, Jaap Vink. Zero art-world presence. Logic actively growing — last commit 2026-06-01.

entries.zh_title: Patchies：所有创作工具的余项在此处做邻居
entries.en_title: Patchies: Where the Remainders of All Creative Tools Become Neighbors
entries.notes: Phoomparin Mano (heypoom), software engineer in Bangkok, Thailand. Works on Metabase embedded analytics by day; builds Patchies solo after midnight. Patchies: open-source creative coding patcher running in browser (patchies.app). 162 GitHub stars, 4143 commits, 6 forks, AGPL-3.0. Built with TypeScript (51.6%), Svelte (37.6%), Rust (2.1% via WASM). Supports 20+ tools from 20+ different creative computing communities on ONE canvas: P5.js, Three.js, HTML5 Canvas, Textmode.js, Hydra, Shader Park, GLSL, Strudel, ChucK, SuperSonic, Bytebeat, Csound, Orca, Pure Data-style audio objects, Tone.js, Elementary Audio, Uxn VM, Assembly, Uiua, Ruby, Python. External connections via MIDI, MQTT, SSE, WebRTC, Iframe, VDO.Ninja. UI widgets via Vue.js, DOM API, Tailwind. Any third-party JS library via esm.sh. Design philosophy: mix textual coding and visual patching — 'write small and compact programs and patch them together.' Builds on earlier projects: Totality Editor, Simulate the Universe, Visual Assembly Canvas (100-day 'From Opcodes to Algorithms'). Co-founded Creatorsgarten (Bangkok creative tech collective, 50+ events since 2017). Collaborations include algorithmic Thai Khon dance performance and visual live-coding with assembly language. Key SAE insight: dual chisel-construct cycle — (1) visual patching (Max/MSP, PD, TouchDesigner, VVVV) is the construct of 'visibility-and-opacity' (see topology, each node opaque); text live coding (TidalCycles, Hydra, SC, Processing) chiseled this into construct of 'precision-and-blindness' (full expression, hidden topology). Patchies chisels BOTH: each node contains visible code AND connections define visible topology. The remainder is the seam between two programming visions — belonging to neither. (2) Cross-community remainder: when data paths traverse Strudel→Hydra→P5→Uxn, each boundary crossing chisels one community's construct, producing computational matter that belongs to no single tradition. The canvas is a gathering place for inter-community remainders. Naming gap: not DAW, not IDE, not visual patcher, not live coding env, not modular synth, not game engine, not notebook — seven naming systems fail. Poom published a 'naming ideas' page in design notes — even the creator can't name it. Inspired by Max, Pd, TouchDesigner, VVVV but diverges by making code the primary content of each node rather than hiding it. Bucket list publicly shared. Community forming on lines forum (llllllll.co). Spoke at WordCamp Asia 2024. Zero art-world presence. Zero gallery representation. Zero institutional backing. Logic actively growing.

entries.zh_title: SonicWeave：为十二平均律不曾命名的声音编写语法
entries.en_title: SonicWeave: Writing Grammar for Sounds That Equal Temperament Left Unnamed
entries.notes: Lumi Pakkanen (frostburn on GitHub), Finnish software engineer with MSc in theoretical physics. Created SonicWeave — a domain-specific programming language for manipulating musical frequencies, ratios, and equal temperaments. Powers Scale Workshop 3 (scaleworkshop.plainsound.org). SonicWeave's primitives are intervals and pitches, not numbers: 3/2 = perfect fifth, 1\12 = one step of 12-TET, sort(3^[-1..5] rdc 2) = Pythagorean major scale. Has control flow, functions, variables, Haskell-style ranges, Python-style semantics, NumPy-like vector ops. CLI, npm package, template tags for embedding in JS/TS. sonic-weave repo: 9 stars, 820 commits, 69 releases, 5 contributors, 64 open issues. scale-workshop repo: 114 stars, 856 commits. Both MIT license. Ecosystem: moment-of-symmetry, xen-midi, ji-lattice, sw-synth, isomorphic-qwerty. Scale Workshop originally by Sevish (Sean Archibald, British microtonal producer) at EUROMicroFest 2017. Pakkanen took over lead dev from v2, designed SonicWeave for v3. Contributors: Vincenzo Sicurella, Lajos Mészáros, Forrest Cahoon, Videco, Kraig Grady. Special thanks: Arsenii 0.5° (co-dev), Inthar (co-dev), Akselai, Godtone, Marc Sabat. Inspired by JS, Python, Haskell, Zig, OCaml, NumPy, Scala format. Triple chisel-construct: (1) 12-TET = Western music's construct since Bach/industrial piano, all other tunings = remainder; (2) Scala format (1992, Manuel Op de Coul) gave remainders notation but is static line-by-line listing, became new construct; SonicWeave chisels Scala's rigidity into programmable scale description; (3) all mainstream PLs treat numbers as arithmetic objects; SonicWeave chisels this assumption — numbers ARE intervals, entire type system built around frequency ratios and cents. Programming language ontology never seen before. Naming gap immense: not a PL (generates tunings not software), not notation (it's code), not calculator (has control flow/functions), not synth/DAW (no direct sound), not math library (primitives are intervals not numbers). PL design community doesn't know it exists. Xenharmonic community knows it but can't categorize. Music tech world barely touches it. Logic still growing. Zero art-world presence.

entries.zh_title: 四千字节里的遗物静物画
entries.en_title: Still Life of Dead Media in Four Thousand Bytes
entries.notes: P_Malin, shader artist under bitshifters collective. Won 1st place 4K Procedural Graphics at Revision 2026 (April 2026) with Lost Media — a still life of obsolete storage media generated from 4096 bytes of shader code. Previous major work: Orders of Magnitude (1st Outline 2022, Meteoriks Best Executable Graphics) — similar concept with floppy disks, SD cards, and a self-referential quine on printed paper. Technique: raymarching signed distance fields, all geometry/materials/lighting purely mathematical. The 4K constraint forces beauty to emerge as a by-product of mathematical compression. Demoscene as aesthetic practice remains a remainder — UNESCO-recognized but not yet fully digested by contemporary art discourse.

entries.project_name: Santhosh Thottingal / Nupuram & Parametric Type Design
entries.zh_title: 当被遗弃的曲线语言复活在马拉雅拉姆文字里
entries.en_title: When an Abandoned Curve Language Resurrects Inside Malayalam Script
entries.notes: Santhosh Thottingal, Wikimedia engineer based in Kerala, India. Since 2020, uses MetaPost (1980s Knuth-lineage drawing language) for modern variable font design — no GUI, pure mathematical formula descriptions of glyphs. Created Nupuram: Malayalam typeface superfamily with 4 variable axes (weight, width, slant, softness). Also created Manjari (spiral splines by Raph Levien). Feb 2026: built custom curve fitting system in Rust based on Raph Levien's two-parameter curve family, replacing Hobby curves. Achieved variable-width stroke outlines that remain interpolatable for variable fonts — solved point-count constancy problem via linear perturbation (B_offset = B + w*D). Multi-stage skeleton-based error correction for G1 continuity at segment joins. Collaborating with Raph Levien and Kurbo team. Triple chisel-construct cycle: (1) MetaPost was Knuth's construct for parametric type design, chiseled away by GUI editors in 1990s, became fossil written in WEB→Pascal; (2) variable font technology (OpenType 1.8) is modern construct assuming GUI-drawn masters — Thottingal finds crevice between two eras; (3) Malayalam script is remainder of Latin-centric font technology — its complex curvature demands expose tool insufficiency. MetaPost Sandbox at mpost.thottingal.in. Published paper 'Parametric type design in the era of variable and color fonts' (arXiv 2502.07386). Next step: building dedicated DSL for type design, inheriting MetaPost spirit. Naming gap: type design community doesn't use MetaPost, MetaPost community is extinct, curve math researchers don't make fonts, Rust/Kurbo is general graphics, Malayalam community needs fonts but not parametric theory. Zero art-world presence. Logic actively growing.

entries.zh_title: 滑轮绘图法：当机械张力成为笔迹
entries.en_title: The Pulley Drawing System: When Mechanical Tension Becomes Stroke
entries.notes: Misha Heesakkers, generative artist from 's-Hertogenbosch NL, completed all 31 days of Genuary 2026. Core system: pulley drawing algorithm where virtual belt wraps around anchor points, path determined by tension/geometry rather than Bézier curves. Used this to build typeface (Day 5), pen-plotter hatching (Day 22), visible-system compositions (Day 18). Also explored cellular automata (Day 9), 3D boxes (Day 12), boolean operations with Clipper.js (Day 7), flow fields (Day 25), recursive hex grids (Day 26), GLSL shaders with Spectral.js (Day 31), HTML-only buttons art (Day 28). SAE insight: belt-and-pulley logic from mechanical engineering transplanted into generative art creates forms that carry memory of physical constraint without obeying physical law. This practice sits in gap between physics simulation art, parametric design, and plotter art - no existing category names it. Active on fxhash and objkt. Sells NFTs and prints. Not in major galleries or institutional art world.

entries.zh_title: XYscope.js：当矢量图形穿越声音抵达荧光
entries.en_title: XYscope.js: When Vector Graphics Travel Through Sound to Reach Phosphor
entries.notes: Ted Davis (ffd8), artist and educator based in Basel, teaches creative coding at FHNW Academy of Art and Design, Switzerland. XYscope originally a Processing library (2017), ported to p5.js ecosystem as XYscope.js (2025, built from scratch). v0.4.7 on GitHub (Dec 2025), 20 stars, GPL-3.0, also on npm. Converts p5.js vector graphics into audio signals that drive analog oscilloscope electron beams to draw shapes on CRT phosphor. Engineering: circle = pair of sine waves 90° out of phase, line = custom wavetable, rectangle = four frequencies. Every stroke is simultaneously a sound; every tone simultaneously a light trace. Can be live-coded in browser via P5LIVE. Key SAE insight: triple domain crossing — signal departs from code (digital coordinates), passes through sound (Web Audio API oscillators with custom wavetables), arrives at light (electron beam tracing phosphor on CRT). At each domain boundary: translation loss and translation gain, artifacts belonging to neither departing nor arriving domain. These are the remainder of the crossing itself. Cartesian separation of image and sound collapses: graphic does not represent sound, sound does not represent graphic — same signal manifesting in different media. This identity is an unnamed aesthetic position. Chisel-construct reversal of oscilloscope: oscilloscope = core construct of 20th-century measurement engineering. Its aesthetics (phosphor afterglow, trace decay, analog warmth) were never designed — byproducts of measurement function, remainder outside engineering purpose. XYscope.js converts oscilloscope from measurement tool to creative medium: foreground of engineering (accurate signal reproduction) becomes background; background (persistence of phosphor glow, analog deflection) becomes foreground. Oscilloscope itself becoming e-waste — remainder of consumer electronics upgrade cycle. New aesthetics on dying hardware adds temporal dimension to remainder. Deeper structure: additive synthesis — multiple XYscope.js instances patched into same audio output, waveforms interfering. Visual result is neither shape A nor shape B — remainder of collision. Tiny frequency differences (50Hz vs 50.1Hz) cause shapes to drift, rotate, breathe — motion quality no digital renderer can replicate. Mathematical interference of two wavetables = pure remainder. Naming gap wide: not music composition tool (no traditional music), not visual art tool (output not on screen), not installation art (runs in browser), not video synthesis (pure vector, no raster), not sound art (sound not the purpose), not creative coding (output not on digital canvas). 'Oscillographics' exists in small practitioner community but art/music/design worlds have no prepared position for triple-domain-identity practice. Logic still growing.

entries.zh_title: Executed Poetry：当代码的两次阅读之间涌现余项
entries.en_title: Executed Poetry: The Remainder That Emerges Between Two Readings of Code
entries.notes: Zeroichi Arakawa (荒川零壱), smart contract engineer and code poet, PhD candidate at IAMAS Japan. Executed Poetry (2025): device with Raspberry Pi Pico W + e-paper display. Press button → Python poem executes inside microcontroller → display shows poem text + execution count + processing time + machine's public key + cryptographic signature (proof of execution). Poems use Python primitives to explore philosophy: 'while True: break' (eternity that never cycles), 'class Void: pass / del Void' (nothingness that persists unnamed), 'assert not self' in finally clause (self-denial proving existence), 'import love' catching ImportError as love (empty heart filled with failure). Key SAE insight: bidirectional chisel-construct — literary tradition chiseled by executability (literature never had this dimension), programming tradition chiseled by poetic meaning (engineering never named this remainder). The remainder exists in the gap between two readings: as literature vs. as code — neither fully captures the work. Execution traces (timestamp, processing time, crypto signature) are physical sediment of computation. Cryptographic signature transforms each execution into unrepeatable event — poem's mode of existence shifts from 'text' to 'event', irreversibility is the remainder. Broader practice: Code Poetry on X (2023-ongoing), CodeTEI (2025, TEI markup for code poetry), BUGCAT (2025), Contract Domino (2025), Mnemonic Poetry (2023, BIP-39 seed phrases as poetry). Exhibited at 'Computational Poetry' exhibition NEORT++ Gallery Tokyo 2025 (co-curated with Yusuke Shono). On Verse.works and fxhash. Naming gap: not concrete poetry (no visual layout concern), not code art (literary quality equally important), not conceptual art (execution is material), not blockchain art (not on-chain), not electronic literature (runs on hardware), not installation art (logic is textual). Category 'executed poetry' still forming. Zero established art-world naming.

entries.zh_title: Glicol：当信号图成为所有乐器的余项
entries.en_title: Glicol: When the Signal Graph Becomes Every Instrument's Remainder
entries.notes: Qichao Lan (chaosprint) created Glicol — a graph-oriented live coding language written from the ground up in Rust, compiled to WebAssembly, running in browsers via AudioWorklet. ~2.9k GitHub stars. Opens at glicol.org with no installation. Every line is a signal chain: 'o: sin 440 >> mul 0.5' — >> is connection, ~ is reference. The entire language does one thing: describe topological relationships between nodes. No timeline, no mixer, no classes, no functions, no variable declarations. Just the graph. Key SAE insight: Glicol's chisel targets not any single construct but the shared assumption of ALL audio systems — that you need an abstraction layer above the signal graph. DAWs hide the graph behind mixer faders, SuperCollider wraps it in OOP, TidalCycles abstracts it into pattern algebra, Sonic Pi encodes it as sequential scripts. Glicol says the graph itself is enough. Remainder = radical transparency where every sound traces to a specific node and connection. Triple cascading remainder in tech stack: Rust (remainder of C++ after ownership/lifetime chisels away GC and undefined behavior), WebAssembly (remainder of native code after sandbox chisels away system calls and platform dependencies), AudioWorklet (remainder of Web Audio API after real-time constraints chisel away main thread and callback hell). Sound passes through three layers of remainder. Naming gap: 'graph-oriented live coding language and music/audio DSP library' — eleven words, every adjacent pair pulls toward a different domain. No single naming system captures it. Still highly experimental, pre-1.0, API may change. Zero art-world presence.

entries.zh_title: sapf：当SuperCollider的创造者凿掉自己的构
entries.en_title: sapf: When SuperCollider's Creator Chisels Away His Own Construct
entries.notes: James McCartney, creator of SuperCollider (1996), open-sourced sapf ('Sound As Pure Form') in January 2025. sapf is a Forth-like language for audio synthesis using lazy lists and APL-like auto-mapping. Postfix notation, stack-based, mostly functional. Represents audio/control events as lazy, possibly infinite sequences. Auto-maps functions over sequences like APL maps over arrays — short programs achieve disproportionate results. Nearly all data types immutable → easy multi-threading. 96kHz default sample rate, spectrogram output, recording to file. Original repo: lfnoise/sapf (934 stars, 26 commits, macOS-only, v0.1.22 Oct 2025). Cross-platform fork: ahihi/sapf (70 stars, 122 commits, Linux/macOS/Windows, Meson build, Nix flake, Docker, CI). Ecosystem: 5 editor plugins (sapf.el for Emacs, two nvim plugins, VS Code extension, LSP server by Vasilii Milovidov), dedicated sapf subforum on scsynth.org, #sapf channel on SuperCollider Discord, video tutorials by Aaron Lanterman and ahihi/pulusound. Inspired by APL, Joy, Haskell, Piccola, Nyquist, SuperCollider. Key SAE insight: deepest form of creator-chisels-own-construct — McCartney built THE construct of academic computer music (SuperCollider: OOP class library, client-server architecture, GUI, IDE, hundreds of UGens, UNESCO-recognized live coding culture), then chiseled it all away to find the minimum: stack + lazy sequences + auto-mapping + postfix. Sound IS the remainder — 'pure form.' Double-remainder lineage: APL (remainder of mathematical notation) + Forth (remainder of programming language design), both 'widely derided as write-only,' combined into new synthesis. Every ecosystem component grown independently by different people — not a product launch but a remainder self-organizing. Naming gap: not SuperCollider (rejects its paradigm), not APL (not arrays), not Forth (has lexical variables), not a synthesizer (it's a language), not a language (it makes sound) — no single name covers it. Zero art-world presence. Zero music technology press coverage. Logic still growing.

entries.zh_title: AMYboard：定点运算的余项里长出了Juno-6的声音
entries.en_title: AMYboard: The Sound of Juno-6 Growing from Fixed-Point Remainder
entries.notes: Brian Whitman (ex-Spotify, variogram.com) and DAn Ellis (Google Research) created AMY — a fixed-point C music synthesis library (~10K lines, 414 GitHub stars, 1883 commits, MIT license) for microcontrollers. Runs on ESP32-S3, Pi, Teensy, Playdate, iOS, web (Emscripten/WASM), Daisy, Godot. Synthesis: Juno-6 analog, DX7 FM, Karplus-Strong, PCM sampler, wavetable, additive partials, 120 voices, 300+ patches, biquad filters, reverb/echo/chorus, pattern sequencer, MIDI management with voice stealing. Fixed-point arithmetic forced by ESP32-S3's lack of fast FPU — accidentally reproduces the sonic character of 1983 hardware (Juno-6/DX7 also used fixed-point). Wire protocol: compact string serialization (v0n50l1K130r0Z) for cross-platform communication. Tulip Creative Computer ($59, shorepine/tulipcc, 858 stars, 2197 commits): handheld device with 7" touchscreen, boots into Python REPL, 120-voice AMY synth, hardware sprites, scrolling BG, MIDI I/O, Wi-Fi, TULIP~WORLD BBS chat, built-in code editor. Also runs on web (tulip.computer/run) and as desktop app. T-Deck port available. AMYboard ($29.90, launched May 18, 2026): 10HP Eurorack, ESP32-S3, analog+S/PDIF audio I/O, MIDI, 2x CV, SD card, I2C, MicroPython firmware, AMYboard online web simulator (same WASM engine). AMYboard World community for sharing sketches. Also powers Diapasonix, Spark, Alles mesh synth. Key SAE insight: triple remainder structure — (1) fixed-point arithmetic is remainder of computational poverty, accidentally producing vintage sonic character; (2) 'creative computer' is a dead category (Amiga/Atari ST died in 1990s), Tulip resurrects it; (3) naming gap is wide open: not commercial synth, not DAW, not Eurorack module, not PC, not game console, not educational product. Each publication names it differently (Synthtopia: 'DIY modular synth', Hackaday: 'MicroPython synth workstation', Hackster: 'Python-powered music computer'). Whitman's personal tone ('hope someone finds it as fun as I have') signals maker-not-company. Still actively developing, adding features 2 years after Tulip launch. Zero art-world presence.

entries.zh_title: CLAVIER-36：当细胞自动机开始为自己作曲
entries.en_title: CLAVIER-36: When Cellular Automata Begin Composing for Themselves
entries.notes: River Dillon (k-monk.org), Recurse Center alumnus. CLAVIER-36 (C36): a live programming language for generative music where programs are laid out in a 2D grid and evolve like cellular automata. Began as from-scratch reimplementation of Orca (by Devine Lu Linvega / Hundred Rabbits), diverged significantly. Key differences from Orca: (1) self-contained instrument with built-in programmable sampler + sine synthesizer (Orca requires external DAW/synth), (2) sample-accurate timing (Orca has timing imprecision Devine discussed on Future of Coding podcast ~41:24), (3) distinguishes operators from literals (Orca doesn't), (4) base-36 numeral system (26 letters + 10 digits = all alphanumeric keys; 36/12 = 3 octaves — 'a happy coincidence'), (5) 36 built-in scales from Major to Diminished, Ryukyu to Bartók Gamma, filling every base-36 address. 27 of 36 operators complete. INTERFERE operator writes symbols into program memory that move autonomously until collision/destruction — projectile composition. Metaprogramming: programs modify themselves at runtime. Evaluation in English reading order (top-to-bottom, left-to-right). Dataflow wiring system added June 2025. MIDI output added July 2025. Steam page created May 2025, planned Early Access release 2026. Listed on Handmade Network. Discord community. Additional web programming by Greg Technology. Language design help from Richard Whaling. SAE insight: nested remainder — (1) Orca chiseled traditional composition, music became remainder of code execution, but Orca became construct over a decade; (2) C36 chisels Orca's construct (external dependency, timing imprecision), absorbs sound pipeline, creates self-sufficient organisms; the 'cost' of self-sufficiency is the remainder — programs that compose autonomously; (3) base-36 alignment between keyboard hardware and musical structure is unplanned bridge between two independent constructs, the remainder of their collision; (4) naming gap: not DAW, not sequencer, not game, not CA simulator, not general programming language — Steam/TOPLAP/Handmade Network each partially claim it but none can fully name it. Still in Early Access, semantics will change, patches may break — the logic is still growing.

entries.zh_title: 单一用途的屏幕：当约束系统走进客厅
entries.en_title: Single-Purpose Screens: When Constraint Systems Walk Into the Living Room
entries.notes: Grant Custer, designer-programmer at Google Creative Lab. Constraint Systems (constraint.systems, 2019-present): 20+ experimental browser-based creative tools each built around a single constraint (Flow: pixel-flows, Type: directed typing, Grid: grid-warped layout). May 2026: started 'Experiments in single-purpose screens' — three dedicated displays in home office. Bottom: Raspberry Pi + Camp Snap screenless camera → looping photo slideshow (no preview = deliberate constraint). Middle: Pi showing full-screen time-block visualizer reading markdown from home server. Top: physical clock with handwritten face and off-the-shelf clock mechanism. Also built: computer box (laptop-as-furniture), album player (Spotify interface showing 6 random albums), music artist info display, ambient TV. Key SAE insight: practice falls in the gap between three already-constructed categories — smart home (construct: seamless/automated), new media art installation (construct: white-cube/spectacle), DIY maker culture (construct: efficiency-maximization). Fits none. Core unresolved contradiction he admits: seeks calm of a digital object that 'is what it is and nothing else' but software can always become something else. No screens have lasted long — 'the unbounded possibilities are still always kind of lurking.' This contradiction is the remainder itself. Uses magnets for removable hardware, smart plugs on schedule (9-6), Tailscale for SSH, Claude Code on Pis for debugging. Feed blog (feed.grantcuster.com) and Scrawl (scrawl.grantcuster.com) document ongoing process. Zero art-world presence for the domestic screen practice. Constraint Systems referenced by IDARESU 2026 (TMU digital humanities workshop) but the physical-screen extension is completely undigested.

entries.zh_title: 互联网基础设施地图：当路由表的余项显影为地理
entries.en_title: Internet Infrastructure Map: When the Routing Table's Remainder Develops into Geography
entries.notes: Kevin McDonald (handle sudorandom), backend engineer. Internet Infrastructure Map at map.kmcd.dev, running since 2022, updated annually. 2026 edition (published Feb 18, 2026) introduces 'Logical Dominance' — a model that layers BGP routing table analysis on top of physical infrastructure (submarine cables + IXPs). Processes 15+ years of BGP RIB snapshots from University of Oregon Route Views and RIPE RIS. Calculates each city's weight by summing originated IPv4 address space. Key SAE insight: Internet's administrative records (WHOIS, IXP registrations, cable catalogues) are the construct; BGP routing table analysis is the chisel; what is exposed is the remainder — the gap between administrative record and routing reality. Discovered 'ghost networks': DoD /8 blocks making Manhattan look like the universe's center, China Telecom's internal routing making Frankfurt appear as China's largest ISP, 0.0.0.0/0 making Australia swallow all IPs. Built 'waterfall attribution logic' (Geofeeds → cloud provider IP lists → BGP Communities → WHOIS → footprint heuristic) — each layer processes the remainder the previous layer couldn't name. Technical: custom on-disk trie using BadgerDB v4 for longest-prefix matching, viewport culling, dynamic cluster grouping, SVG export, permalink state encoding. Exposed raw JSON datasets for community use. Sits between network engineering, cartography, infrastructure criticism, and data aesthetics — none can fully name it. Zero art-world presence. Annual evolution ensures the logic keeps growing.

entries.zh_title: TugPhonon：当1951年的磁盘开始生长共振体
entries.en_title: TugPhonon: When a 1951 Magnetic Disk Begins Growing Resonators
entries.notes: Tuğrul Akyüz (handle tugrulakyuz, brand 2Rule), independent plugin developer. TugPhonon v1.0.0 released April 20, 2026: free software recreation of the 1951 Phonogène rotating magnetic disk delay by Jacques Poullin and Pierre Schaeffer (GRM Paris). Eight independent playback heads on virtual rotating disk with delay, volume, pan, feedback per head. Key innovation: physical modeling resonators attached to each head output — Karplus-Strong, Comb, Bell, Pipe, Marimba, Beam, Membrane — based on Bessel functions, Euler-Bernoulli beam theory, measured bell partial ratios. Also: tremolo, ring modulation, LFO per head, bandpass filter, tape saturation, variable tape loop length, head spread control. Developer calls it a 'sound transformation instrument,' not a delay. SAE insight: nested double chisel-construct cycle — (1) tape recording construct (faithful reproduction) chiseled to expose temporal remainder (multi-head delay/displacement), (2) temporal remainder as excitation fed into physical model construct (acoustic equations), producing resonant remainder (decay, ringing, nonlinear behavior equations can't fully predict). Sound passes through two chisel-construct cycles. Broader practice: TugSpect (image pixel values → FFT spectral filtering of audio), TugImgSynth (image → playable wavetable), TugGlicento (multi-effect matrix), 2RuleSynth, 2RuleFilter, SynthTrack, TugMidiSeq. Pattern: each plugin builds an impossible instrument that harvests remainder when a signal crosses into an alien domain. All free on Gumroad. Wix-hosted personal site with default social links and PayPal donate button. Zero art-world presence. Four naming systems fail: VST community (free experimental effect), musique concrète (Phonogène archaeology), physical modeling DSP (engineering), sound art (doesn't know plugin devs exist). None can name what he does.

entries.zh_title: Cagire：当Forth的栈成为音乐的余项
entries.en_title: Cagire: When Forth's Stack Becomes the Remainder of Music
entries.notes: Raphaël Maurice Forment (BuboBubo), French musician and PhD in musicology (Jean Monnet University, 2025, thesis on live coding aesthetics). Created Cagire v0.1.6 (2026): a step sequencer where each step contains a Forth script instead of note data. When the sequencer reaches a step, it runs the script. Music is the remainder of code execution. Forth (Charles Moore, 1970) is the remainder of programming language evolution — stack + words + numbers, no syntax, postfix notation. Key SAE insight: triple chisel-construct cycle — (1) Forth is the remainder of programming language history (all abstraction layers chiseled away, only the stack remains), (2) the step sequencer grid is the construct of electronic music (TR-808 paradigm: grid=note); Cagire replaces notes with arbitrary code, making music the remainder of execution, (3) Forment's own tool-making trajectory is successive reduction: Sardine (Python, 2022) → Topos (TypeScript) → Sova (polyglot) → Cagire (Forth, absolute minimum). Each tool chisels the previous. Cagire is the remainder of this reduction sequence. Also runs as VST3/CLAP plugin inside DAWs — a Forth interpreter parasitizing commercial music production infrastructure. Built-in audio engine Doux (Rust port of Felix Roos's Dough). Supports 32 banks × 32 patterns × 1024 steps, Ableton Link sync, MIDI I/O. AGPL-3.0. Terminal + desktop + plugin versions. Self-hosted on Gitea. Active in TOPLAP and Cookie Collective (Paris). Zero art-world presence. Sits between live coding, electronic music production, programming language archaeology, and instrument-building — none can fully name it.

entries.zh_title: compute.toys：当片段着色器的疆界之外开始涌现生命
entries.en_title: compute.toys: When Life Emerges Beyond the Fragment Shader's Frontier
entries.notes: compute.toys is a WebGPU-based compute shader playground ('Shadertoy for compute shaders'). Uses Slang shading language transpiled to WGSL, runs in browser. 181 GitHub stars, 777 commits, small active community. Key SAE insight: Shadertoy (2013) established fragment shader art as the construct — one function per pixel, stateless, eternal images. compute.toys chisels away this paradigm's limitations, exposing the GPU's computational remainder: compute shaders with read-write buffers, persistent state, atomic operations, arbitrary thread dispatch. This enables fundamentally different beauty: particle systems with memory, fluids that flow between frames, agent-based emergent phenomena, temporal/evolving aesthetics. The tech stack itself layers remainders: Slang (NVIDIA research) + WGSL (W3C standard) + WebGPU (browser vendor competition) — no single community owns this combination. Sits between GPU programming, creative coding, demoscene, scientific visualization, and web art — none can fully name 'compute shader art' as a distinct medium. WebGPU only broadly available since 2023-2024; Safari 26 added support in 2026. The practice is in its earliest days. Zero art-world recognition of compute shaders as a distinct creative medium.

entries.zh_title: css-doodle：层叠样式表里未被命名的生成力
entries.en_title: css-doodle: The Unnamed Generative Force Inside Cascading Style Sheets
entries.notes: Yuan Chuan (Chinese web developer) built css-doodle — a tiny web component (~6k GitHub stars) that generates a grid of empty divs controllable with pure CSS. No Canvas, no WebGL, no JS bindings. Creates kaleidoscopic lattices, gradient tapestries, fractal textures, animated sculptures using only browser layout features (Grid, transforms, gradients, clip-path, animations, custom properties, trig functions). Key SAE insight: CSS's entire history is a chisel-construct cycle — W3C/browser vendors build features as construct (for web layout), css-doodle chisels away the 'web page' purpose, exposing the pure mathematical generative power latent in declarative syntax as remainder. Trig functions stop calculating positions and draw spirals; Grid stops arranging columns and becomes visual crystal lattice substrate; gradients stacked 12 layers deep produce unpredicted textures. Second layer: CSS itself is the 'remainder layer' of the web's tripartite structure (HTML=structure, JS=behavior, CSS=presentation/decoration) — historically dismissed as 'not real programming.' css-doodle proves this dismissed decorative layer harbors an entire unexcavated aesthetic stratum. Still actively evolving: April 2026 multi-stroke text effects research, shader integration, experimental SVG syntax. Each CSS spec expansion opens new remainder veins. Lives on CodePen/GitHub, zero art-world naming. Not generative art (no NFTs/minting), not web design (no client), not creative coding (Processing/p5.js communities ignore pure CSS). Remainder identity still alive.

entries.project_name: Kiran Scott de Martinville / Are.na Frame
entries.zh_title: Are.na Frame：当数字策展的物理沉积物开始闪烁
entries.en_title: Are.na Frame: When the Physical Sediment of Digital Curation Begins to Flash
entries.notes: Kiran Scott de Martinville (industrial designer, London/SF) created Are.na Frame: open-source color e-ink display (Spectra 6, six pigments) that cycles through Are.na channel contents. Released April 23, 2026, limited edition of 40, hand-assembled; full open-source hardware/assembly guide available. Key SAE insight: the transition flash between images — where six pigment layers are built up sequentially like spot-color printing — is the visible remainder of the e-ink chisel-construct cycle (old image chiseled, new constructed, flash is the interstitial state belonging to neither). Deeper layer: Kiran's great-great-great-great-great-grandfather Édouard-Léon Scott de Martinville invented the phonautograph (1857), the first sound recording device — designed to SEE sound, not play it back. The recording was an unnamed remainder for 148 years until decoded in 2005. Are.na Frame has perfect structural symmetry: also a device for seeing (turning invisible digital curation into physical sediment). E-ink's charged pigment particles physically moving in cells mirror sound waves etching soot-paper. Also experimenting with distributed mode loudspeakers and Chladni plate cymatics with light/lasers — continuing ancestral 'seeing sound' lineage. Sits between product design, installation art, open-source hardware, infrastructure criticism, and physical manifestation of digital curation — none can fully name it. Charles Broskoski (Are.na co-founder) partnership. Zero art-world naming.

entries.zh_title: Spectrum Slit：当电磁场成为无人感知的余项
entries.en_title: Spectrum Slit: When the Electromagnetic Field Becomes an Unperceived Remainder
entries.notes: rootkid (anonymous, hacker handle) created Spectrum Slit (January 2026): a sculptural installation using SDR to continuously scan 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz bands, mapping signal strength in real time onto 64 LED filaments. Each filament = one spectrum slice, brightness = electromagnetic intensity. The sculpture becomes a temporal portrait of collective digital behavior — surging during streaming, dimming at night, flickering with each message. Materials: aluminum, microcomputer, custom electronics, SDR, LED filaments. Key SAE insight: electromagnetic field IS the remainder of wireless communication — the chisel-construct cycle of modern networking treats data integrity as construct, the physical EM wave as disposable carrier/waste. No one designs the beauty of a room's EM field. Spectrum Slit performs a chisel-construct reversal: background (EM waste) becomes foreground, foreground (data protocols) becomes invisible. rootkid has only 4 works total, no gallery representation. Other works include Exhibit A (functional darknet marketplace activated by button press — crime as medium), Whispering Wires (1960s telephone plays AI-processed poetry), Latent Reflection. Practice sits between sculpture, data viz, infrastructure criticism, electromagnetic art (Kubisch tradition), and surveillance art. Zero art-world naming. YouTube video: moBCOEiqiPs.

entries.zh_title: window-art：当窗口框架成为画布的余项
entries.en_title: window-art: When the Window Frame Becomes the Canvas's Remainder
entries.notes: willmeyers released window-art v0.1.1 on March 14, 2026. A minimal Python library for live coding visual scenes using desktop windows themselves as the medium — create, move, resize, recolor, fade windows with smooth animations and 24+ easing functions. Can also display images, video, and text in windows. 71 GitHub stars, 11 commits, 3 contributors, pure Python. Key SAE insight: double remainder — (1) every creative coding framework treats 'drawing inside a window' as construct; window-art chisels that away, exposing the window frame/chrome as remainder; (2) the desktop windowing paradigm itself is dying (phones, tablets, fullscreen web have no windows), so the window manager is the remainder of a vanishing interaction model. References JODI's 1990s desktop disruption tradition but domesticates it into a composable, live-codable instrument. HN commenter noted even the demoscene never questioned the window — it's a blind spot because it's too fundamental. Sits between creative coding, demoscene, net art, and desktop art — none can fully name it. Zero art-world presence.

entries.zh_title: Headless Hydra：当图形栈被凿尽，视觉在废弃设备上复活
entries.en_title: Headless Hydra: When the Graphics Stack Is Chiseled Away, Visuals Resurrect on Discarded Devices
entries.notes: Gábor L Ugray (gugray), Berlin-based generative artist, co-founder of memoQ, background in CS and linguistics. Created Headless Hydra — a zero-dependency Go program that reimplements Olivia Jack's Hydra visual live coding environment without WebGL, without a browser, without X11. Writes pixels directly to framebuffer via SSH on systems with no display manager. Runs on 2016 Samsung phone with PostmarketOS, second-hand Raspberry Pi connected to CRT TV via composite video. Presented at LGM 2026 (Libre Graphics Meeting, Nuremberg) on April 25, 2026. Also performed 'Godshatter' at ICLC 2025 Barcelona, 'Equinox' at TOPLAP Winter Solstice 2023. Ongoing pen plotter practice since 2021, exhibited at Phasenpunkte/Hilbertraum Berlin 2024. Key SAE insight: double chisel-construct cycle — (1) Hydra's infrastructure (browser/WebGL/GPU/X11) is construct; chiseling it away leaves the computational remainder of visual synthesis, a Go program writing pixels one-by-one; (2) the devices themselves are remainder of consumer electronics' upgrade cycle, resurrected as creative sites. Explicitly framed as resistance against centralized computation and as permacomputing practice. Sits between live coding, permacomputing, systems programming, and video art — none can fully name it. Still evolving. Zero art-world presence.

entries.zh_title: Soup of Life：当作者退场后，进化本身成为余项
entries.en_title: Soup of Life: When the Author Exits, Evolution Itself Becomes the Remainder
entries.notes: Soup of Life: continuously running open-ended artificial life simulation at soupof.life. Anonymous creator. No goals, no player control, no optimization loops — organisms evolve autonomously through mutation, inheritance, and lineage divergence. Morphology, physiology, cognition, and behavior encoded as mutable traits. Intelligence has explicit energy cost creating oscillation between simple/complex strategies. Procedural terrain, climate variation, resource gradients create ecological niches. Emergent behaviors include predator-prey arms races, parasitic strategies, cooperative symbioses, boom-bust cycles, extinction cascades, adaptive radiations — none programmed. Users observe and export 'life cards.' ISAL encyclopedia entry added March 2026 by Anya Vostinar. Hacker News discussion. Instagram community sharing organism cards. Key SAE insight: evolution IS the chisel-construct cycle (mutation=chisel, adaptation=construct, surviving organisms=remainder). Deeper layer: creator's deliberate withdrawal makes the system an authorless remainder-production machine. Beauty is undesigned — it is the remainder of computation. Sits between game art, generative art, interactive art, computational biology, digital ecology — none can name it. Currently transitioning from independent experiment to academic recognition but not yet art-world-named.

entries.zh_title: cuneus：当心理学家用着色器捕捉知觉的余项
entries.en_title: cuneus: When a Psychologist Captures Perception's Remainder in Shaders
entries.notes: Enes Altun (altunenes), psychologist + Rust developer. Two interlinked projects: rusty_art (growing collection of optical illusions and generative art in Rust) and cuneus (custom GPU compute shader engine built on wgpu/egui/winit, published on crates.io). Implements research-grade optical illusions (Munker, Café Wall, Pinna, Adelson checker shadow, lilac chaser, Leviant, Gabor patches, Asahi, reverse phi motion, cafewall) as real-time WGSL shaders with GUI parameter controls. Key SAE insight: optical illusions ARE the remainder of the visual system's chisel-construct cycle — they occur at exact nodes where edge detection, color constancy, or motion processing fails, producing perceptual artifacts the brain cannot stably digest. Second-layer remainder: shader computation faithfully reproduces human perceptual failure without itself being fooled — the gap between mathematical computation and human perception is itself a remainder. cuneus born from Nannou's abandonment — remainder of an orphaned dependency. Supports multi-pass rendering, atomics, hot reload, WASM export, GPU audio synthesis (generate music from WGSL), 3D Gaussian splatting, video/webcam input. Also maintains sorceress (Python/JS optical illusions with neuroscience citations). Sits between visual neuroscience, GPU systems programming, creative coding, and psychophysics — none can fully name it. Active development, v0.4.6+. Zero art-world presence.

entries.zh_title: graffito：当细胞自动机拒绝意义之后
entries.en_title: graffito: What Remains When Cellular Automata Refuse Meaning
entries.notes: Niels G. W. Serup (nqpz), Copenhagen-based programmer with MSc from DIKU. graffito is a cellular automaton framework written in Futhark (data-parallel functional GPU language from DIKU). Explicitly creates 'pretty cellular automata devoid of meaning' — refuses to simulate reality. Each stencil (steal, coralreef, routefinder, collatz, etc.) is a set of local rules producing emergent global patterns on GPU via OpenCL. Key SAE insight: the chisel operation is removing 'simulation of reality' from the cellular automata construct — what remains is pure visual emergence, the remainder. Tool choice is itself remainder: Futhark was designed for compiler research, not art; the alignment between data-parallel semantics and stencil computation is accidental affinity. Stencils generate unplanned results: routefinder 'ended up being more about building mountains', consistencyfier labeled 'Not sure yet'. Framework is open for contributions. Talks at BornHack 2024 and FOSDEM 2026. Zero art-world presence. Sits between compiler research, GPU computing, creative coding, generative art, and demoscene — none can fully name it. 3 years of quiet development on GitHub.

entries.zh_title: Our Shiver：当雾凿掉互联网
entries.en_title: Our Shiver: When Fog Chisels Away the Internet
entries.notes: Carrie Hott (interdisciplinary artist, Assistant Professor at Indiana University Eskenazi School). Our Shiver: solar-powered website on DIY server at The Lab, SF. Solar panel on Redstone Building roof at 37° angle. Single HTML file, server only runs when battery has charge — SF fog takes it offline. Three-year residency, first artist commissioned to explore The Lab's digital environment. Key SAE insight: fog is literal chisel in chisel-construct cycle; sun deposits energy (construct), fog removes it (chisel), website's intermittent existence is the remainder. Makes visible the hidden material dependency of all digital infrastructure. Also co-stewards 'how to slow internet' project with 'cicada' experiment (social site updating every 17 days). Sits between net art, installation art, infrastructure criticism, permacomputing, environmental art — none can fully name it. Featured on IPM Nice Work podcast Feb 27 2026. 2017 Artadia Award recipient.

entries.zh_title: heerich.js：当雕塑变成减法的余项
entries.en_title: heerich.js: When Sculpture Becomes the Remainder of Subtraction
entries.notes: David Aerne (meodai), Swiss interaction developer known for color-names (30K+ hand-named colors), Poline, RampenSau. Released heerich.js March 2026: zero-dependency JS engine for 3D voxel scenes → SVG. Named after Erwin Heerich (1922-2004), German sculptor of geometric cardboard forms. Boolean ops (union/subtract/intersect/exclude) on integer voxel grid, then oblique/perspective/orthographic/isometric projection to SVG polygons. Remainder at two levels: (1) voxelization is lossy quantization of continuous space — staircase aliasing is the grid's signature; (2) SVG output is projection residue — 3D crushed into painter's algorithm depth-sorted quads. removeGeometry literally chisels: carved faces are boolean remainder, not drawn but exposed. Occlusion culling mode for pen plotters: polygons clipped by all in front, zero-overlap output = ultimate sediment layer. Per-voxel scale transforms, decals (bilinear-warped SVG paths on faces), GPURenderer for Three.js, content voxels, findByPosition hit-testing. Philosophy: 'what if we spent less time making individual decisions and more time designing how decisions get made?' — remainder logic. Sits between voxel art, generative art, pen-plotter community, sculptural thinking, front-end development — none can fully name it. Active development, weekly features. MIT license.

entries.zh_title: Small64：当整台机器只剩余项
entries.en_title: Small64: When the Entire Machine Becomes Remainder
entries.notes: First ever Nintendo 64 4K intro (4096 bytes total ROM). By Rasky, HailToDodongo, Phire, Pestis. Entire demo is the bootloader — must init RAM, decompress itself before RAM exists, pass N64 secure boot checksum via GPU brute-force. Uses random garbage in RAM as metallic texture, harvests undefined bits in MIPS opcodes for hash cracking free variables. Music synth carved from 8-instrument/reverb/delay to 4-channel/single-oscillator/no-effects because N64 CPU can't keep up. Custom section reordering tool 'swizzle' using simulated annealing for compression optimization. Won Meteoriks 2026 Outstanding Technical Achievement. Key SAE insight: beauty IS the remainder — what survives extreme compression is the structural minimum, and the structural minimum is beautiful. Multiple naming gap: demoscene (UNESCO heritage but not art-world-named), N64 homebrew (remainder of game dev), 4K intro (remainder of the remainder). The entire machine becomes nothing but remainder.

entries.zh_title: L5：六兆字节里的余项复活术
entries.en_title: L5: Resurrecting the Remainder in Six Megabytes
entries.notes: Lee Tusman (Associate Professor of New Media & CS at SUNY Purchase, co-organizer of Permacomputing NYC meetups) built L5 — a ~6MB creative coding library implementing the Processing API in Lua on Love2D. Designed to run on old/discarded hardware (decade-old laptops, outdated phones, Raspberry Pis). Key SAE insight: reverse chisel-construct operation — the tech industry's cycle turns hardware from remainder to construct (e-waste), L5 reverses this by making condemned machines into living creative sites again. Choice of Lua (born 1993 Brazil, extreme backward compat, near-zero evolution speed) is a temporal remainder strategy — betting on 'longest' not 'newest'. In early alpha, GSoC project via Processing Foundation, talk at xHain Berlin April 19 2026. Sits between permacomputing, creative coding, sustainable design, educational tech, indie games — none can fully name it.

entries.zh_title: Variograph：当图像是变换函数的沉积物
entries.en_title: Variograph: When the Image Is Sediment of Composed Transformations
entries.notes: Etienne Jacob (bleuje), Paris-based software engineer. Variograph is a real-time generative drawing tool using openFrameworks and compute shaders. Core algorithm: compose 'variation' functions (from fractal flame algorithms) — each maps 2D→2D. Millions of particles pass through the composed function chain and are plotted as near-transparent dots; the image is trail sediment, not drawn. Has 3D mode (2D→4D→3D→2D projection chain). Used as installation with gamepad at 5+ events. Also has interactive-physarum project (building on Sage Jenson's 36 Points). Key SAE insight: the remainder is mathematical — cascading positional displacements through composed functions. The tool resists mastery ('getting interesting results is not really easy the more you become used to the tool'). Sits between fractal art, generative art, installation art, mathematical visualization — not yet named as a category. Open source GPL v3, available on itch.io.

entries.zh_title: 10,000 Drum Machines：节奏作为数据的余项
entries.en_title: 10,000 Drum Machines: Rhythm as the Remainder of Data
entries.notes: Maxwell Neely-Cohen's growing collection of 40+ browser-based drum machines, each converting non-musical data (USGS earthquake feeds, De Bruijn sequences, logic gates, cat images) into rhythm via step sequencers. Rhythm is the remainder of data forced through a sequencer grid. The '10,000' target is a structural horizon ensuring permanent incompletion — the project is designed as an apparatus for continuous remainder accumulation. Philosophy: 'saturate the web with esoteric musical instruments' against slop. Collaborator Jessie Char (Seismic Drum Machine). 'Ground Loops' live installation at Pittsburgh Cultural Trust. Open-source on GitHub. Covered by CDM, Adafruit, kottke.org. Not yet named by art world — falls between sound art, net art, data sonification, and open-source tooling.

entries.zh_title: Alex McLean：从活代码到活织物，余项的逆向凿构
entries.en_title: Alex McLean: From Live Code to Live Cloth — The Remainder's Reverse Chisel
entries.notes: Creator of TidalCycles (the most important live coding music language) now physically weaving on an 8-shaft table loom, exploring crackle weave — algorithmic threading patterns where a motif repeats along a path with rule-based intermediate steps. Double-direction remainder: algorithm→material (thread tension/slippage as physical remainder the code can't predict) and material→algorithm ((un)weaving workshop in April 2026 where participants reverse-engineer finished cloth back into threading structures). UKRI Future Leaders Fellowship project 'Algorithmic Pattern' (Alpaca) asks how ancient/traditional pattern-making rethinks creative technology design. Connected to PENELOPE project (weaving as origin of algorithmic thinking, with Ellen Harlizius-Klück). Not claimed by textile art, media art, or craft revival — sits in the gap between live coding, textile research, mathematics, and archaeology.

entries.zh_title: Trpti Sanghvi：地铁闸机数据里的群飞余项
entries.en_title: Trpti Sanghvi: The Murmuration Remainder Inside Turnstile Data
entries.notes: NYC-based creative technologist (Odissi dancer + product analyst) who mapped MTA subway turnstile data onto starling murmuration/flocking algorithms for Data Through Design 2026 Echo(logies) at BRIC House, Brooklyn (March 21-April 5, 2026). Double-remainder structure: turnstile data is the remainder of commuting behavior, murmuration pattern is the remainder of agent rules. The collision produces forms that belong to neither transit planning nor biology. Her embodied/dance background gives her a non-standard perspective on data flows. Not yet categorizable as data viz, bioart, or urban art.

entries.zh_title: humanbydefinition：字符栅格中的有损余项
entries.en_title: humanbydefinition: The Lossy Remainder Inside the Character Grid
entries.notes: Anonymous creator (handle humanbydefinition, email 'travellingwithoutarriving'). Built three interconnected projects: p5.asciify (real-time ASCII conversion for p5.js via WebGL2 shaders), textmode.js (framework-agnostic textmode rendering engine), and synth.textmode.art (live coding environment for procedural ASCII synthesis). The structural remainder: continuous visual space is force-translated into a character grid at 60fps — the ASCII residue is a byproduct of lossy compression, not a goal. Sits between ASCII art history, demoscene tradition, creative coding community, and live-coding lineage — claimed by none. Featured on CreativeApplications.Net. Not yet named as a category by the art world.

entries.zh_title: GPenT：当图像只是指令的余项
entries.en_title: GPenT: When the Image Is Just the Remainder of an Instruction
entries.notes: Teddy Warner's GPenT is a wall-mounted polargraph pen plotter with a full open-source software pipeline. Key feature: dcode generator, a diffusion model trained to convert text directly to G-code, skipping the image step entirely. The image is a remainder of executed machine instructions, not a goal. System uses Gemini to shuffle/select combinations of multiple generators (procedural, image-upload, ML). Multi-layered remainder production: text→generator combination→G-code→physical drawing. Not yet categorizable as AI art, plotter art, or conceptual art — sits in the gaps. Featured on Hackaday and Adafruit Feb 2026.

entries.zh_title: Andrei Jay：视频反馈作为余项的乐器制造
entries.en_title: Andrei Jay: Building Instruments for the Remainder of the Loop
entries.notes: Mathematician and video artist who built the Video Synthesis Ecosphere (VSERPI) — an open-source platform of interchangeable video synthesis instruments running on Raspberry Pi. Includes WAAAVE_POOL (framebuffer delay/feedback), AUTO_WAAAVE (audio-reactive feedback), SPECTRAL_MESH (chaotic video oscillators), PHOSPHORM (audiovisual synth for oscilloscope). The remainder is structural: video feedback is literally frame-residue accumulation. Not gallery art but instrument-building — a site of continuous remainder production. Community growing (Pi 5 ports, guides). NES analogy: same hardware, swap the cartridge.

entries.zh_title: Jawhar Kodadi：当zellige的几何密码进入算法
entries.en_title: Jawhar Kodadi: When Zellige's Geometric Code Enters the Algorithm
entries.notes: Rabat-based architect who translates traditional Moroccan zellige geometric craft into parametric code (Grasshopper/Rhino) and browser tools (p5.js). Zellige EVO series and free online Zellige Pattern Generator/Creator. The remainder is what happens when centuries-old geometric rules run in algorithmic space — variations no craftsman would make but that grow from the same logic. Not yet named by art world as a category.

entries.zh_title: deconbatch：事故编程法，或余项如何自己写代码
entries.en_title: deconbatch: The Accidental Programming Method, or How the Remainder Writes Its Own Code
entries.notes: Anonymous Japanese creative coder who runs 'Land of 1000 Creative Codings' blog. Proposed the Accidental Programming Method: change parameters thoughtlessly, swap operators, treat bugs as discoveries. De Jong attractor jellyfish shapes found by hand-tuning. Perlin noise bug produced superior aesthetics. All code open source. No gallery/NFT/curatorial presence. The method itself is a remainder-production mechanism.

entries.zh_title: LB Allix：从氰版到绘图仪，余项的迁徙
entries.en_title: LB Allix: From Cyanotype to Plotter, the Migration of the Remainder
entries.notes: Paris-based artist who moved from cyanotype photography to pen plotter generative art. The entry focuses on how chemical contingency migrates into algorithmic contingency, and how daily practice itself is a structural remainder. Architecture and spatial design background gives her a non-programmer approach to generative line work.

entries.zh_title: Landlines Art：代码出错之后
entries.en_title: Landlines Art: After the Code Misfires
entries.notes: Generative artist driven by accidental coding mistakes. Key work: Sedimentary Dissolution (512 pieces, interactive erosion algorithms). Featured at The Generative Art Museum (TGAM). Collectors can manipulate works via keystroke — completion itself stays open.
